docs.title: QuranKit --- Arabic Text Standard
docs.text:
Document status: Initial technical standard\ Version: 0.1.0\ Scope: Arabic text ingestion, preservation, normalization, tokenization, matching, and display

This document defines how QuranKit handles Arabic text, especially Qur'anic text. It is intended to prevent accidental loss of orthographic information and to ensure that search, comparison, and linguistic analysis remain reproducible.

This is a technical data-handling standard. It does not determine which Qur'anic orthography, reading, or scholarly position is religiously authoritative. Those choices must be tied to identified sources and documented editions.

docs.title: 1. Goals
docs.text:
QuranKit must:

  1. Preserve source text exactly as imported.
  2. Support more than one orthographic representation, including Uthmani and Imlai where reliable data is available.
  3. Make every normalization operation explicit and versioned.
  4. Keep exact-text comparison separate from search-oriented matching.
  5. Avoid confusing orthographic similarity with lexical, morphological, or semantic identity.
  6. Preserve the ability to trace a match back to its original source characters.
  7. Handle Arabic Unicode and combining marks correctly.
  8. Support word-level research without assuming that whitespace always defines a linguistic word.
  9. Make transformations reproducible across machines and software versions.

docs.title: 2. Non-negotiable rules
docs.text:
• Never overwrite source Arabic text with normalized text.
  • Never silently remove diacritics, Quranic marks, hamza distinctions, or pause signs from the stored original.
  • Never describe a normalized match as an exact source-text match.
  • Never convert Uthmani text to Imlai text without identifying the conversion rules and version.
  • Never infer a root, lemma, reading, or grammatical analysis from normalization alone.
  • Never merge different qira'at or text editions into one undifferentiated text field.
  • Never assume that visually similar Unicode strings are byte-identical or code-point-identical.
  • Every derived text representation must identify its source record and transformation profile.

docs.title: 3. Text layers
docs.text:
Keep the following layers conceptually and physically separate.

Layer Purpose Example use

Source text Exact imported Archival fidelity and representation citation

Display text Optional presentation User interface adjustments rendering

Search-normalized text Search-oriented Diacritic-insensitive equivalence lookup

Linguistic Token, lemma, Grammar and lexical representation morphology, or research segmentation data

Transliteration Romanized Optional display or representation accessibility

Translation Translation in a named Meaning exploration language and edition

A display transformation must not become the archival source. A search-normalized string must not be used as a substitute for a linguistic analysis. A translation must never replace the Arabic source text.

docs.title: 4.1 Encoding
docs.text:
• Store text as Unicode.
  • Use UTF-8 for text files and interchange formats unless a documented format requires otherwise.
  • Validate decoding during ingestion.
  • Reject or quarantine malformed input rather than silently replacing invalid bytes.
  • Record the source encoding and any decoding conversion where known.

docs.title: 4.2 Unicode normalization
docs.text:
Unicode normalization forms can change code-point sequences while preserving canonical or compatibility equivalence. QuranKit should not apply compatibility normalization indiscriminately to source text.

Recommended policy:

  • Preserve the exact decoded source string in text_original.
  • A derived processing representation may use NFC when justified and documented.
  • Do not apply NFKC or NFKD to Qur'anic source text by default.
  • Record the normalization form in the transformation profile.
  • Test behavior with combining marks and Arabic presentation forms.

Unicode normalization is not the same as Arabic orthographic normalization. NFC does not decide whether two Arabic spellings should be treated as equivalent for a particular research task.

docs.title: 4.3 Offsets
docs.text:
Character offsets must have a documented convention.

Recommended default:

  • Store offsets as zero-based Unicode code-point offsets into the exact text_original string.
  • Use an exclusive end offset: [start, end).
  • Do not mix byte offsets, UTF-16 code-unit offsets, grapheme-cluster offsets, and code-point offsets.
  • If an external corpus uses a different offset convention, preserve its original offsets separately and provide a verified mapping.

Because Arabic letters may contain combining marks, a visible grapheme can contain multiple code points. User-interface cursor positions may therefore require grapheme-aware handling even when database offsets use code points.

docs.title: 5. Arabic character and mark categories
docs.text: Do not implement normalization as an undocumented list of global string replacements. Define and test categories.

docs.title: 5.1 Base letters
docs.text: Preserve base Arabic letters in source text. Search profiles may optionally equate selected forms, but each equivalence must be named and documented.

docs.title: 5.2 Hamza and alif forms
docs.text:
Potentially relevant forms include:

  • ا
  • أ
  • إ
  • آ
  • ٱ
  • ء
  • ؤ
  • ئ

These forms are not universally interchangeable. A search profile may offer a broad hamza-insensitive mode for discovery, but exact and linguistically careful modes must retain distinctions.

Do not remove hamza distinctions from the original. Do not assume that hamza normalization is appropriate for morphology, qira'at, or orthographic research.

docs.title: 5.3 Alif maqsurah and ya
docs.text: The forms ى and ي may be treated as equivalent by a configurable broad-search profile in selected use cases. They must remain distinct in source text and in exact orthographic comparison.

docs.title: 5.4 Ta marbutah and ha
docs.text: The forms ة and ه must not be globally equated. A broad user-facing search may optionally support a candidate expansion, but results must disclose that the match used a relaxed equivalence.

docs.title: 5.5 Diacritics and recitation marks
docs.text:
Arabic text can include marks for:

  • Short vowels.
  • Tanwin.
  • Shaddah.
  • Sukun.
  • Madd and other recitation-related signs.
  • Superscript or small letters.
  • Quranic annotation and pause signs.

Do not assume every combining mark is optional decoration. Some marks encode pronunciation, reading, or textual conventions.

A profile that removes selected vowel marks must identify exactly which Unicode characters it removes. It must not remove all combining marks indiscriminately.

docs.title: 5.6 Quranic annotation and pause signs
docs.text:
Pause signs, sajdah markers, rub' markers, and other Quranic annotations may be encoded as characters, combining marks, or separate metadata depending on the source.

Recommended policy:

  • Preserve them in the source layer.
  • Identify their role where the source specification permits.
  • Expose separate search options for including or excluding annotation marks.
  • Do not remove them from the source string during import.
  • Where marks are stored as structured metadata instead of inline characters, retain the original source representation or a documented reversible mapping.

docs.title: 6. Normalization profiles
docs.text:
Normalization must be selected by name and version. A profile is a documented transformation contract, not an informal label.

The following profiles are proposed starting points. Their exact character mappings must be specified and tested before implementation.

docs.title: 6.1 exact-source-v1
docs.text:
Purpose: exact comparison with the selected source representation.

Rules:

  • No Arabic letter substitutions.
  • No diacritic removal.
  • No Quranic mark removal.
  • No whitespace collapsing unless the comparison mode explicitly excludes surrounding transport whitespace.
  • Preserve the exact source string.

Use for source fidelity and exact edition-specific comparison.

docs.title: 6.2 canonical-unicode-v1
docs.text:
Purpose: a limited Unicode canonical normalization for processing.

Rules:

  • Apply NFC to a derived copy only.
  • Do not apply Arabic letter equivalences.
  • Do not remove diacritics or Quranic marks.
  • Preserve the original source string independently.

Use only when canonical Unicode equivalence is needed.

docs.title: 6.3 diacritics-insensitive-v1
docs.text:
Purpose: discover text matches regardless of a defined set of vocalization marks.

Rules:

  • Start from a derived copy.
  • Remove only an explicit allowlist of marks designated by the profile.
  • Retain base letters and hamza distinctions.
  • Retain Quranic annotation marks unless the profile explicitly defines their handling.
  • Return the original source text and indicate that diacritic-insensitive matching was used.

Do not call this profile "unvocalized exact text"; it is a relaxed match.

docs.title: 6.4 search-broad-v1
docs.text:
Purpose: broad discovery for user-entered Arabic queries.

May include configurable options for:

  • Selected alif/hamza equivalences.
  • Selected alif maqsurah/ya equivalence.
  • Removal of a specified set of vowel marks.
  • Optional handling of tatweel.
  • Optional whitespace and punctuation normalization.

Rules:

  • Every enabled transformation must be visible in the profile configuration.
  • Return match type and applied transformations.
  • Do not use this profile for claims about exact spelling, qira'at, or morphology.
  • Do not make ta marbutah/ha equivalence a default.

docs.title: 6.5 Custom profiles
docs.text:
Allow users to define custom profiles, but require:

  • A unique profile identifier.
  • A version.
  • Explicit rules.
  • A deterministic implementation.
  • Tests and documentation.
  • A clear statement of intended use.

A profile change that alters results must receive a new version.

docs.title: 7. Suggested normalization pipeline
docs.text:
A search pipeline should be ordered and inspectable.

Input query
   |
   v
Validate Unicode
   |
   v
Select explicit profile
   |
   v
Apply configured Unicode normalization
   |
   v
Apply configured Arabic mark handling
   |
   v
Apply configured letter equivalences
   |
   v
Apply whitespace/punctuation policy
   |
   v
Search matching index
   |
   v
Return original source text + match metadata

The pipeline should not apply a linguistic root or lemma transformation unless the user explicitly selects a morphological search operation and a suitable annotation dataset is available.

docs.title: 8. Uthmani and Imlai representations
docs.text:
Uthmani and Imlai representations should be modeled as distinct text representations or editions, not as a single field with an implicit conversion.

For every supported representation, record:

  • Dataset and version.
  • Source and edition details.
  • Script/orthography description.
  • Reading information where relevant.
  • Text coverage and known limitations.
  • Tokenization convention.
  • License and redistribution status.

A conversion between representations must record:

  • Input edition.
  • Output representation.
  • Conversion rules and version.
  • Characters or signs omitted, substituted, or expanded.
  • Whether the mapping is reversible.
  • Known ambiguities.

Do not claim that a conversion is fully reversible unless tested and demonstrated. Prefer loading a separately sourced representation when one is available and appropriately licensed.

docs.title: 9.1 Do not equate whitespace tokens with linguistic words
docs.text:
Whitespace splitting may be useful as an initial text segmentation method, but Arabic orthography and morphology can involve attached clitics, particles, and other segmentation choices.

QuranKit should distinguish:

  • Text span: a sequence of source characters.
  • Orthographic token: a unit under a specified tokenization convention.
  • Morphological segment: a clitic or morpheme-level component.
  • Linguistic word: a unit defined by a linguistic annotation scheme.

docs.title: 9.2 Tokenization metadata
docs.text:
Every tokenization scheme must document:

  • Source corpus or algorithm.
  • Version.
  • Treatment of attached conjunctions, prepositions, articles, and pronouns.
  • Treatment of punctuation and Quranic marks.
  • Whether token boundaries are source-provided or computed.
  • Offset convention.
  • Known limitations.

docs.title: 9.3 Stable token identity
docs.text:
A token identifier must include or reference:

  • Text edition.
  • Surah and ayah.
  • Tokenization scheme and version.
  • Token position or source identifier.

Do not reuse token IDs across different tokenization schemes merely because the visible surface strings happen to match.

docs.title: 9.4 Segmentation alignment
docs.text: When a source provides morphological segments, store the alignment from segments to the parent orthographic token and source character span. Preserve the source's segmentation labels and provide a mapping layer if QuranKit uses a normalized tagset.

docs.title: 10. Search modes and result labeling
docs.text:
Every search operation should expose its matching mode.

Mode What it matches Result label

Exact source Same source exact_source_match representation

Canonical Unicode Canonically normalized unicode_normalized_match representation

Diacritic-insensitive Match after specified diacritic_insensitive_match mark removal

Broad orthographic Match under configured broad_orthographic_match letter equivalences

Token sequence Ordered token sequence token_sequence_match

Lemma Sourced lemma lemma_match annotation

Root Sourced root annotation root_match

Fuzzy Approximate string fuzzy_candidate similarity

Semantic Model or vector semantic_candidate similarity

Do not combine these into one undifferentiated search score.

A result should include:

  • Original source reference.
  • Original matched text.
  • Query as supplied.
  • Normalized query.
  • Normalization profile and version.
  • Match mode.
  • Dataset and edition.
  • Character/token alignment where available.
  • Any ambiguity or limitation.

docs.title: 11. Display and rendering
docs.text:
• Use a font with adequate Arabic and Quranic glyph coverage.
  • Preserve logical Unicode text order in storage.
  • Use a rendering environment that supports right-to-left layout and bidirectional text.
  • Do not manually reverse Arabic strings for display.
  • Test mixed Arabic, Latin, numbers, punctuation, and verse references.
  • Ensure copy/export operations return the intended source representation.
  • Do not silently replace source text with a font-specific or presentation-form encoding.

Display should be tested in the actual target interfaces, because browser, terminal, PDF, and notebook rendering may differ.

docs.title: 12. Transliteration
docs.text:
Transliteration is a derived representation.

If supported:

  • Identify the transliteration standard or scheme.
  • Version the implementation.
  • Preserve source-to-output alignment where practical.
  • Do not present transliteration as a replacement for Arabic.
  • Distinguish scholarly transliteration from simplified pronunciation aids.
  • Do not infer a single pronunciation where qira'at or reading information is not specified.

docs.title: 13. Import and validation requirements
docs.text:
Every text importer must:

  1. Record source, dataset version, edition, and license metadata.
  2. Preserve exact decoded source strings.
  3. Validate Unicode.
  4. Verify surah and ayah references.
  5. Detect duplicate and missing records.
  6. Preserve source identifiers.
  7. Record tokenization source and version.
  8. Validate character offsets against the source string.
  9. Avoid implicit normalization during import.
  10. Produce a report of errors, warnings, and coverage.

Do not silently "repair" malformed Arabic. Any repair process must create a separate derived value and retain the original.

docs.title: 14. Test strategy
docs.text: Build tests around reviewed examples and source fixtures.

docs.title: Unicode tests
docs.text:
• NFC and NFD behavior.
  • Combining mark sequences.
  • Arabic presentation forms.
  • Invalid input handling.
  • Code-point offsets and grapheme behavior.

docs.title: Orthographic tests
docs.text:
• Hamza and alif forms.
  • Alif maqsurah and ya.
  • Ta marbutah and ha.
  • Tatweel.
  • Diacritics.
  • Quranic annotation and pause marks.

docs.title: Search tests
docs.text:
• Exact source matching.
  • Diacritic-insensitive matching.
  • Broad search equivalences.
  • No accidental equivalence in exact mode.
  • Result metadata and source offsets.

docs.title: Tokenization tests
docs.text:
• Token boundaries.
  • Clitic segmentation.
  • Multiple tokenization versions.
  • Source alignment.
  • Empty or malformed tokens.

docs.title: Regression tests
docs.text: Every discovered normalization or segmentation bug should receive a minimal fixture and a regression test. Fixtures must be traceable to their source and must not be fabricated Qur'anic text.

docs.title: 15. Proposed API shape
docs.text:
The following is illustrative and does not define final signatures:

from qurankit import QuranKit

quran = QuranKit()

# Exact source search
results = quran.search(
    "query",
    mode="exact",
    edition="selected-edition",
)

# Search with a named normalization profile
results = quran.search(
    "query",
    mode="orthographic",
    normalization="diacritics-insensitive-v1",
)

# Retrieve the unchanged source text
ayah = quran.ayah("2:255", edition="selected-edition")
original = ayah.text_original

The API should make it difficult to accidentally use broad normalization when exact comparison is intended.

docs.title: 16. Open decisions
docs.text:
Before implementation, resolve and document:

  1. Which source text edition is the initial reference edition?
  2. Which Uthmani and Imlai sources are available and redistributable?
  3. Which Unicode characters are classified as vocalization marks versus Quranic annotation marks in each source?
  4. Which normalization profiles are required for the first alpha?
  5. Which tokenization corpus or convention is used initially?
  6. What offset convention does each imported corpus use?
  7. How are qira'at and orthographic variants represented in a later extension?
  8. Which fonts and rendering environments are included in visual regression testing?

Do not invent mappings to close these gaps. Keep uncertain transformations opt-in until verified against source specifications and reviewed examples.

docs.title: 17. Recommended implementation order
docs.text:
1. Implement source-preserving text ingestion.
  2. Add Unicode validation and source checksums.
  3. Add exact-source-v1 search.
  4. Add one explicitly specified diacritic-insensitive profile.
  5. Add a reviewed tokenization adapter.
  6. Add Uthmani/Imlai source adapters when source data and licensing are verified.
  7. Add broad orthographic search as an opt-in profile.
  8. Add morphological search only after reliable annotations are integrated.
  9. Add rendering tests for supported interfaces.

This order prioritizes textual integrity before convenience features.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: QuranKit provides a command-line interface for dataset management, search, and textual analysis.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install qurankit-core[cli]
qurankit --help

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
qurankit [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:
  --version  Show the version and exit.
  --help     Show this message and exit.

docs.title: qurankit data list
docs.text:
List available datasets.

qurankit data list                    # All datasets
qurankit data list --installed-only   # Only installed

docs.title: qurankit data install
docs.text:
Install a dataset.

qurankit data install tanzil          # Install Tanzil text
qurankit data install qac             # QAC morphology (manual download required)
qurankit data install tanzil --force  # Force reinstall

docs.title: qurankit data validate
docs.text:
Validate an installed dataset's checksums.

qurankit data validate tanzil

docs.title: qurankit data manifest
docs.text:
Show or export dataset manifest.

qurankit data manifest tanzil
qurankit data manifest tanzil -o manifest.json

docs.title: qurankit ayah
docs.text:
Get ayah text and word tokens.

qurankit ayah "2:255"
qurankit ayah "1:1" -e "tanzil-uthmani-v1"

docs.title: qurankit surah
docs.text:
List surahs or get surah details.

qurankit surah              # List all 114 surahs
qurankit surah -s 1         # Surah Al-Fatihah details

docs.title: qurankit editions
docs.text:
List available text editions.

qurankit editions

docs.title: qurankit search
docs.text:
Search for text in the Qur'an.

qurankit search "بسم الله"
qurankit search "الرحمن" -m exact
qurankit search "رحمة" -m broad -l 50

Modes: - exact — Exact source text match - diacritic-insensitive — Ignore vocalization marks (default) - broad — Broad orthographic matching - canonical — Unicode NFC normalization only

docs.title: qurankit mutashabihat
docs.text:
Find repeated phrases for an ayah.

qurankit mutashabihat "2:255"
qurankit mutashabihat "1:1" --min-length 3

docs.title: qurankit ngrams
docs.text:
Find recurring n-grams across the corpus.

qurankit ngrams --n 3 --min-occurrences 2
qurankit ngrams -n 2 -e "tanzil-uthmani-v1"

docs.title: qurankit report
docs.text:
Generate detailed mutashabihat comparison report.

qurankit report "2:255" -m exact
qurankit report "2:255" -m near-duplicate --threshold 0.8
qurankit report "2:255" -m normalized --profile "search-broad-v1"

docs.title: qurankit corpus-stats
docs.text:
Corpus-level mutashabihat statistics.

qurankit corpus-stats

docs.title: qurankit research semantic-relations
docs.text:
Find semantic relations from dictionary sources.

qurankit research semantic-relations "ر ح م" --type synonym
qurankit research semantic-relations --lemma "رحمة" --type antonym
qurankit research semantic-relations "ك ت ب" --type all

Types: synonym, antonym, related, all

docs.title: qurankit research collocations
docs.text:
Compute corpus-wide collocations.

qurankit research collocations --top 50 --measure pmi
qurankit research collocations -w 10 --min-cooc 5 --measure dice
qurankit research collocations --no-stopwords

Measures: pmi, t_test, dice, log_likelihood, frequency

docs.title: qurankit research collocations-for
docs.text:
Get collocations for a specific word.

qurankit research collocations-for "الْحَمْدُ" --top 20
qurankit research collocations-for "رحمن" -w 5 --measure log_likelihood

docs.title: qurankit research cross-refs
docs.text:
Find cross-references for an ayah.

qurankit research cross-refs "2:255" --implicit
qurankit research cross-refs "2:255" --explicit
qurankit research cross-refs "2:255" --implicit --min-roots 3 --limit 30

docs.title: qurankit research wujuh-wa-nazair
docs.text:
Find wujuh wa nazair candidates.

qurankit research wujuh-wa-nazair "2:255" --limit 20
qurankit research wujuh-wa-nazair --limit 100  # Corpus-wide
qurankit research wujuh-wa-nazair "2:255" --min-shared 2 --threshold 0.5

docs.title: qurankit profiles
docs.text:
List available normalization profiles.

qurankit profiles

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install data
qurankit data install tanzil

# Search
qurankit search "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم"

# Get ayah
qurankit ayah "2:255"

# Find repeated phrases
qurankit mutashabihat "2:255"

# Research
qurankit research collocations --top 20
qurankit research cross-refs "2:255" --implicit

docs.title: Research Workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Find collocations for a key term
qurankit research collocations-for "رحمن" --measure pmi --top 15

# 2. Find related verses by shared vocabulary
qurankit research cross-refs "2:255" --implicit --limit 10

# 3. Check for wujuh wa nazair
qurankit research wujuh-wa-nazair "2:255" --limit 15

# 4. Get detailed mutashabihat report
qurankit report "2:255" -m normalized --min-length 3

docs.title: Dictionary Research
docs.text:
# Find synonyms from Lane's Lexicon / Al-Mufradat
qurankit research semantic-relations "ر ح م" --type synonym
qurankit research semantic-relations --lemma "رحمة" --type all

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
• 0 — Success
  • 1 — General error
  • 2 — Invalid command/arguments

docs.title: QuranKit --- Data Model
docs.text:
Document status: Initial design proposal\ Version: 0.1.0\ Applies to: QuranKit core text-first research framework

This document defines the initial logical data model for Qur'anic text, word-level records, linguistic annotations, lexical resources, dataset provenance, and computational research results.

It is a design specification, not a claim that these tables or APIs have already been implemented. The schema should evolve through reviewed migrations as real datasets are evaluated.

docs.title: 1. Design goals
docs.text:
The data model must:

  1. Preserve every imported source representation without destructive modification.
  2. Give surahs, ayat, and word tokens stable, unambiguous references.
  3. Support multiple text editions, orthographies, tokenizations, and readings without conflating them.
  4. Represent lexical and linguistic analyses as sourced annotations, not unquestionable facts.
  5. Preserve multiple competing analyses where the data supports them.
  6. Make dataset provenance and licensing traceable down to individual records or annotation batches.
  7. Support deterministic search and computational analysis.
  8. Remain usable in a local SQLite installation, with a path to PostgreSQL later.
  9. Avoid requiring an LLM, vector database, graph database, or hosted service.

docs.title: 2.1 Separate canonical structure from text editions
docs.text:
The Qur'anic reference 2:255 identifies surah 2, ayah 255. It does not, by itself, identify a particular digital text representation.

A text edition identifies the source and representation of the text. Different editions may differ in orthography, symbols, metadata, or tokenization. Store them separately.

docs.title: 2.2 Preserve original data
docs.text:
For each imported text or annotation, retain:

  • The original value as received.
  • The source and dataset version.
  • The source record identifier, if available.
  • The transformation applied during import.
  • The transformed value used internally, if any.

Never replace original Arabic text with normalized text.

docs.title: 2.3 Distinguish a word token from a linguistic word analysis
docs.text:
A token is a specific occurrence in a specific text edition and tokenization. Its root, lemma, part of speech, and grammatical role are analyses attached to that occurrence.

One token may have multiple analyses. A root may be unknown, disputed, or absent from a source. Do not force every token to have one.

docs.title: 2.4 Distinguish lexical meaning from contextual interpretation
docs.text: A dictionary entry is not the same thing as the meaning of a word in a particular ayah. Model dictionary definitions, occurrence-level notes, semantic relations, and scholarly interpretations separately.

docs.title: 2.5 Make provenance first-class
docs.text: A result should be traceable to the dataset, edition, source, method, and software version that produced it.

docs.title: 3. Entity relationship overview
docs.text:
The central relationships are:

Source ──< Dataset ──< DatasetRecord
                    │
                    ├── TextEdition ──< AyahText ──< WordToken
                    │                                  │
                    │                                  └──< TokenAnalysis
                    │
                    ├── LexicalResource ──< LexicalEntry
                    │                            │
                    │                            └──< LexicalSense
                    │
                    └── AnnotationSet ──< Annotation

Surah ──< Ayah
Ayah ──< AyahMetadata
WordToken ──< TokenLexicalLink >── LexicalEntry
ResearchRun ──< ResearchResult
ResearchRun ──< ResearchInput

The diagram is conceptual. A first SQLite implementation may use fewer physical tables, provided it preserves these distinctions and can migrate cleanly.

docs.title: 4. Core identifiers
docs.text:
Use explicit, documented identifiers.

Object Suggested identifier Example

Surah surah_number 2

Ayah (surah_number, ayah_number) 2:255

Text edition edition_id uthmani-example-v1

Ayah text (edition_id, surah_number, ayah_number) Edition-specific 2:255

Word token token_id uuid or stable composite key

Dataset dataset_id + version corpus-name@1.0.0

Lexical entry lexical_entry_id Source-preserving identifier

Annotation annotation_id uuid

Research run run_id uuid

A word token should be tied to a text edition and a tokenization version. A simple display reference such as 2:255:3 may be offered to users, but it must not be treated as globally stable across all editions and tokenization schemes.

Recommended human-readable reference:

<edition_id>:<surah>:<ayah>:<tokenization_id>:<token_index>

Example:

uthmani-example-v1:2:255:tok-v1:3

The example is illustrative only.

docs.title: 5.1 Source
docs.text:
Represents the bibliographic or digital origin of a dataset.

Field Type Notes

source_id string, primary key Internal stable ID

title string Source title

creator string, nullable Author, organization, or maintainer

source_type enum/string Corpus, book, API, manuscript, database, etc.

url string, nullable Source location

persistent_id string, nullable DOI or other persistent identifier

publisher string, nullable Publisher or issuing body

publication_year integer, nullable Do not infer if unknown

notes text, nullable Bibliographic or evaluation notes

One source may provide multiple datasets or editions.

docs.title: 5.2 Dataset
docs.text:
Represents an importable, versioned data release.

Field Type Notes

dataset_id string, primary key Stable dataset name

version string Source release/version

source_id foreign key Originating source

name string Display name

description text Contents and intended use

license_id string, nullable SPDX identifier or documented custom license

license_url string, nullable License text

redistribution_status enum allowed, restricted, unknown, not_redistributable

retrieved_at datetime, nullable Retrieval timestamp

checksum_algorithm string, nullable For example sha256

checksum string, nullable Checksum of source artifact

schema_version string Import schema version

language string, nullable BCP 47 or documented language code

metadata_json JSON, nullable Additional source metadata

Do not treat unknown redistribution status as permission to redistribute.

docs.title: 5.3 DatasetRecord
docs.text:
Optional but recommended when individual imported records need their own provenance.

Field Type Notes

dataset_record_id string, primary key Internal record ID

dataset_id foreign key Dataset release

source_record_id string, nullable Original record key

record_type string Text, lexical entry, annotation, etc.

record_checksum string, nullable Hash of original record

raw_payload text/JSON, nullable Original payload if storage policy permits

imported_at datetime Import timestamp

For large datasets, store raw source artifacts separately and retain a stable path or object key plus checksum.

docs.title: 5.4 Surah
docs.text:
Represents the canonical surah index.

Field Type Notes

surah_number integer, primary key 1--114 name_arabic text Name from a selected reference source name_transliteration text, nullable Display metadata name_translation text, nullable Display metadata ayah_count integer Validate against selected structure metadata_source_id foreign key, nullable Source of metadata

Names and descriptive metadata should be source-attributed. Do not assume that one transliteration or translation is canonical.

docs.title: 5.5 Ayah
docs.text:
Represents the canonical location of an ayah, independent of a specific digital text edition.

Field Type Notes

surah_number integer, primary key Foreign key to Surah part

ayah_number integer, primary key Local ayah number part

global_ayah_number integer, nullable Common sequence number if adopted

metadata_json JSON, nullable Additional sourced structural metadata

Primary key: (surah_number, ayah_number).

docs.title: 5.6 TextEdition
docs.text:
Represents a text source, orthographic representation, or reading edition.

Field Type Notes

edition_id string, primary key Internal stable identifier

dataset_id foreign key Dataset providing the text

name string Edition name

script_type string For example Uthmani or Imlai

reading_id string, nullable Qira'ah/riwayah identifier when applicable

orthography string, nullable Source description

tokenization_id string, nullable Tokenization scheme/version

is_default boolean Default display edition, not a claim of universal authority

notes text, nullable Differences and known limitations

Do not merge qira'at into a single text field. Represent readings and their source-specific variants explicitly when that scope is implemented.

docs.title: 5.7 AyahText
docs.text:
Stores the exact ayah string for a particular edition.

Field Type Notes

edition_id foreign key, primary Text edition key part

surah_number integer, primary key Canonical location part

ayah_number integer, primary key Canonical location part

text_original text Exact source string

text_display text, nullable Display-only transformation, if needed

source_record_id string, nullable Original record identifier

checksum string, nullable Integrity check

metadata_json JSON, nullable Source-specific metadata

text_original must not be rewritten by search normalization, typography, or display formatting.

docs.title: 5.8 WordToken
docs.text:
Represents a token occurrence in a particular ayah text and tokenization.

Field Type Notes

token_id string, primary key Stable internal ID edition_id foreign key Text edition surah_number integer Ayah location ayah_number integer Ayah location tokenization_id string Segmentation scheme/version token_index integer Position within ayah under this scheme surface_original text Exact token as segmented from source char_start integer, nullable Offset into source ayah text char_end integer, nullable Exclusive end offset source_record_id string, nullable Source token ID segmentation_notes text, nullable Notes about segmentation

Constraints:

  • Unique (edition_id, surah_number, ayah_number, tokenization_id, token_index).
  • Foreign key to the matching AyahText.
  • Offsets must use a documented convention, such as Unicode code-point offsets into text_original.
  • Do not assume a token is always equivalent to a morphological word. Clitics and segmentation conventions may differ.

docs.title: 5.9 NormalizationProfile
docs.text:
Defines a named and versioned text transformation.

Field Type Notes

profile_id string, primary key For example search-v1 name string Human-readable name version string Profile version description text Intended use rules_json JSON Explicit transformations and options implementation_version string Code version created_at datetime Creation timestamp

A normalized token or ayah string may be cached for performance, but it must reference the profile and source text it was derived from.

docs.title: 5.10 LexicalResource
docs.text:
Represents a dictionary, lexicon, or vocabulary source.

Field Type Notes

lexical_resource_id string, primary key Internal ID

dataset_id foreign key Dataset release

title string Work or resource title

author string, nullable Author/compiler

edition string, nullable Edition information

language string Entry language

scope string, nullable General Arabic, Qur'anic vocabulary, etc.

notes text, nullable Editorial notes

docs.title: 5.11 LexicalEntry
docs.text:
Represents a dictionary headword or lexical record.

Field Type Notes

lexical_entry_id string, primary key Internal ID

lexical_resource_id foreign key Source lexicon

source_entry_id string, nullable Original entry key

headword_original text Exact source headword

headword_normalized text, nullable Search helper only

root_form text, nullable Only when source explicitly supplies or supports it

entry_text_original text, nullable Original entry text

entry_location text, nullable Volume/page/entry reference

metadata_json JSON, nullable Additional source data

docs.title: 5.12 LexicalSense
docs.text:
Separates multiple meanings or senses within an entry.

Field Type Notes

sense_id string, primary key Internal ID

lexical_entry_id foreign key Parent entry

sense_number integer, nullable Source ordering

definition_original text Source wording

definition_language string Language tag

gloss text, nullable Short gloss; identify if editorial

usage_note text, nullable Source-provided note

source_location text, nullable Page or section

editorial_status string Source text, edited transcription, etc.

Do not silently rewrite classical dictionary definitions. If a modern summary is added, store it separately and identify it as an editorial or generated gloss.

docs.title: 5.13 Root and Lemma
docs.text:
Root and lemma are distinct linguistic concepts and should not be represented by one overloaded field.

Root

Field Type Notes

root_id string, primary key Internal identifier root_form text Arabic root representation root_normalized text, nullable Search helper notes text, nullable Editorial notes

Lemma

Field Type Notes

lemma_id string, primary key Internal identifier lemma_form text Lemma representation lemma_normalized text, nullable Search helper language string Language tag notes text, nullable Editorial notes

A token's connection to a root or lemma belongs in its analysis record, because analyses may differ.

docs.title: 5.14 TokenAnalysis
docs.text:
Represents one analysis of a token from a named source or method.

Field Type Notes

analysis_id string, primary key Internal ID

token_id foreign key Analyzed token

dataset_id foreign key, nullable Source dataset, if imported

root_id foreign key, nullable Root candidate

lemma_id foreign key, nullable Lemma candidate

part_of_speech string, nullable Source tag or mapped tag

morph_features_json JSON Inflectional and derivational features

segmentation_json JSON, nullable Morpheme/clitic structure if available

method_type enum/string source_annotation, human_review, algorithmic

confidence number, nullable Only if meaningful and documented

is_preferred boolean Project curation choice, not absolute truth

notes text, nullable Ambiguity and rationale

If confidence is stored, document what it means. Do not compare confidence values from unrelated models or annotation sources as though they were calibrated identically.

docs.title: 5.15 GrammarAnalysis
docs.text:
Represents syntax, i'rab, or other grammar annotations.

Field Type Notes

grammar_analysis_id string, primary key Internal ID

token_id foreign key, nullable Token-level annotation

ayah_text_key foreign key, nullable Ayah-level annotation

dataset_id foreign key, nullable Source

analysis_type string Nahwu, i'rab, dependency, etc.

role_label string, nullable Source's grammatical role

parent_token_id foreign key, nullable Dependency relation if applicable

explanation_original text, nullable Source explanation

method_type string Source, reviewed, algorithmic

metadata_json JSON, nullable Source-specific details

A grammar annotation may apply to a phrase or ayah rather than one token. A later implementation may introduce a general annotation-target table to handle spans and groups.

docs.title: 5.16 SemanticRelation
docs.text:
Represents a sourced or explicitly computed relationship between lexical or conceptual objects.

Field Type Notes

semantic_relation_id string, primary key Internal ID

subject_type string Lexical entry, lemma, concept, etc.

subject_id string Subject identifier

relation_type string Synonym, antonym, related concept, etc.

object_type string Target entity type

object_id string Target identifier

dataset_id foreign key, nullable Source

method_type string Source annotation, human review, algorithmic

evidence_note text, nullable Supporting evidence

confidence number, nullable Documented if used

Do not encode a relationship as a scholarly fact when it is only a model suggestion or vector-neighbor result.

docs.title: 5.17 AyahMetadata
docs.text:
Stores sourced structural or descriptive metadata separately from the canonical ayah location.

Examples include juz, hizb, rubu', page, ruku', Makki/Madani classification, revelation order, and other study metadata.

Field Type Notes

ayah_metadata_id string, primary key Internal ID surah_number integer Ayah location ayah_number integer Ayah location metadata_type string juz, page, revelation_order, etc. value_text text Flexible value representation dataset_id foreign key Source source_reference text, nullable Page, section, or record notes text, nullable Disagreement or caveat

Some metadata applies to ranges of ayat rather than individual ayat. A future AyahRange entity may be preferable for range-based structure. Do not duplicate range metadata onto every ayah without recording the original range semantics.

docs.title: 5.18 Annotation
docs.text:
A general-purpose annotation entity for data that does not fit a specialized table.

Field Type Notes

annotation_id string, primary key Internal ID target_type string Ayah, token, span, lexical entry, etc. target_id string Target identifier annotation_type string Topic, rhetoric, note, variant, etc. content_original text, nullable Source wording content_structured_json JSON, nullable Structured annotation dataset_id foreign key, nullable Source dataset method_type string Source, human review, algorithmic review_status string Unreviewed, reviewed, disputed, etc.

A general annotation should not replace specialized, queryable entities such as TokenAnalysis or LexicalSense.

docs.title: 6.1 ResearchRun
docs.text:
Records an executed research operation.

Field Type Notes

run_id string, primary key Unique run

operation string Search, comparison, frequency, similarity, etc.

algorithm_name string Method identifier

algorithm_version string Version

parameters_json JSON Exact parameters

normalization_profile_id string, nullable Profile used

software_version string QuranKit version

started_at datetime Run timestamp

completed_at datetime, nullable Completion timestamp

status string Completed, failed, partial

environment_json JSON, nullable Relevant runtime details

docs.title: 6.2 ResearchInput
docs.text:
Links a research run to its inputs.

Field Type Notes

research_input_id string, primary key Internal ID run_id foreign key Research run input_type string Ayah, token, dataset, query, etc. input_reference text Stable reference dataset_id foreign key, nullable Dataset version used

docs.title: 6.3 ResearchResult
docs.text:
Stores or indexes the output of a research run.

Field Type Notes

result_id string, primary key Internal ID

run_id foreign key Producing run

result_type string Exact match, similarity candidate, statistic, etc.

claim_category string Source annotation, deterministic result, suggestion, hypothesis

result_payload_json JSON Structured result

evidence_json JSON, nullable Supporting references

limitations text, nullable Known caveats

For large outputs, store result files separately and keep a URI/path, checksum, and schema version in the record.

docs.title: 7. Search data model
docs.text:
Search should operate on indexed derived fields while retaining a path to source text.

Possible derived indexes:

  • Exact source text index.
  • Diacritic-insensitive text index.
  • Named normalization-profile index.
  • Token surface index.
  • Lemma index.
  • Root index.
  • Lexical headword index.
  • Phrase and n-gram index.

Every search request should declare:

  • Target scope: ayah, token, lexical entry, or all supported.
  • Text edition(s).
  • Search mode.
  • Normalization profile.
  • Whether diacritics matter.
  • Whether matching is exact, prefix, fuzzy, morphological, or semantic.

Search results should include the original source text and stable references, not only normalized strings.

Semantic search is optional and must be labeled as candidate discovery. Store embedding model, model version, text input, and vector-index version if embeddings are added.

docs.title: 8. Mutashabihat and comparison model
docs.text:
Do not store all similarity as one generic score. Record the comparison method and evidence.

A comparison result should be able to represent:

  • Exact phrase overlap.
  • Shared token sequence.
  • Near-duplicate sequence.
  • Shared lemma or root.
  • Word-order difference.
  • Insertion, deletion, or substitution.
  • Similar opening or ending.
  • Semantic candidate relationship.

Suggested logical record:

Field Type Notes

comparison_id string, primary key Comparison identifier

left_reference text Ayah or span reference

right_reference text Ayah or span reference

comparison_method string Exact, token edit distance, lemma overlap, etc.

method_version string Algorithm version

normalization_profile_id string, nullable Used profile

score number, nullable Method-specific score

alignment_json JSON Matched and differing spans/tokens

claim_category string Usually deterministic result or suggestion

review_status string Unreviewed, reviewed, disputed

run_id foreign key Reproducibility link

A similarity score must never be presented as proof that two ayat have the same meaning or interpretation.

docs.title: 9. Suggested SQLite implementation
docs.text:
Start with relational tables and foreign keys. Use SQLite features conservatively so migration to PostgreSQL remains feasible.

Recommended initial choices:

  • INTEGER for numeric canonical indices.
  • TEXT for Arabic text and identifiers.
  • ISO 8601 UTC timestamps for stored timestamps.
  • JSON stored as TEXT with validation in application code, or SQLite JSON functions where available.
  • Foreign-key enforcement enabled on every connection.
  • Explicit unique constraints and indexes.
  • FTS5 for full-text search, with separate indexes for separate normalization profiles.

Potential indexes:

CREATE INDEX idx_ayah_text_location
ON ayah_text (surah_number, ayah_number);

CREATE INDEX idx_word_token_location
ON word_token (
    edition_id,
    surah_number,
    ayah_number,
    tokenization_id,
    token_index
);

CREATE INDEX idx_token_analysis_root
ON token_analysis (root_id);

CREATE INDEX idx_token_analysis_lemma
ON token_analysis (lemma_id);

CREATE INDEX idx_lexical_entry_headword
ON lexical_entry (headword_normalized);

These are illustrative. Final SQL must match the implemented schema and migration system.

docs.title: 10. Data validation rules
docs.text:
Every dataset importer should validate:

  1. Required metadata and license status are present or explicitly unknown.
  2. Source and dataset identifiers are stable.
  3. Surah and ayah references are valid for the selected structure.
  4. Duplicate records are detected.
  5. Text is valid Unicode and original values are preserved.
  6. Word token indices are ordered and unique within their tokenization.
  7. Character offsets follow the documented convention and remain within the source string.
  8. Foreign keys resolve.
  9. Normalized fields identify the profile and implementation version.
  10. Imported annotations retain source record identifiers where available.

Validation reports should distinguish errors, warnings, and informational messages. An importer must not silently discard invalid records.

docs.title: 11. Example records
docs.text: The following examples are structural illustrations. They do not provide Qur'anic quotations or assert a particular linguistic analysis.

docs.title: Ayah text record
docs.text:
{
  "edition_id": "example-edition-v1",
  "surah_number": 2,
  "ayah_number": 255,
  "text_original": "<exact source text stored here>",
  "source_record_id": "source-specific-record-id",
  "checksum": "sha256:..."
}

docs.title: Word token record
docs.text:
{
  "token_id": "example-token-id",
  "edition_id": "example-edition-v1",
  "surah_number": 2,
  "ayah_number": 255,
  "tokenization_id": "example-tokenization-v1",
  "token_index": 1,
  "surface_original": "<exact token from source>",
  "char_start": 0,
  "char_end": 8
}

docs.title: Token analysis record
docs.text:
{
  "analysis_id": "example-analysis-id",
  "token_id": "example-token-id",
  "dataset_id": "example-corpus",
  "root_id": null,
  "lemma_id": null,
  "part_of_speech": null,
  "morph_features_json": {},
  "method_type": "source_annotation",
  "confidence": null,
  "is_preferred": false
}

Null values are intentional when the source does not provide an analysis.

docs.title: 12. Migration and versioning policy
docs.text:
• Version the database schema independently from the package version.
  • Use explicit, ordered migrations.
  • Never mutate imported source artifacts as a migration side effect.
  • Make migrations testable on both empty and populated databases.
  • Preserve identifiers or provide explicit mapping tables when identifiers change.
  • Record the dataset and schema versions used to build a local database.
  • Provide a validation command after dataset import or migration.
  • Keep a rollback or recovery strategy for destructive schema changes.

docs.title: 13. Decisions to resolve before implementation
docs.text:
The following choices require a documented decision:

  1. Which digital Qur'anic text edition is the first supported source?
  2. Which source provides canonical surah and ayah metadata?
  3. Which tokenization convention is adopted first?
  4. Are token IDs UUIDs, deterministic hashes, or composite identifiers?
  5. Which Unicode offset convention is used?
  6. Which morphology corpus is supported first, and what is its license?
  7. Which lexical resources may be redistributed?
  8. Which metadata belongs in core tables versus source-specific JSON?
  9. Which schema migration tool will be used?
  10. Which fields are required for a first alpha release?

Do not finalize the schema around hypothetical datasets. Evaluate actual source formats and licenses, then adapt the import model while preserving the principles in this document.

docs.title: 14. Recommended implementation order
docs.text:
1. Implement Source, Dataset, and dataset manifest validation.
  2. Implement Surah, Ayah, TextEdition, and AyahText.
  3. Add a verified text importer and integrity checks.
  4. Implement WordToken with a documented tokenization scheme.
  5. Add normalization profiles and derived search indexes.
  6. Add lexical-resource and lexical-entry adapters.
  7. Add token morphology and grammar annotations.
  8. Add research-run and result provenance.
  9. Add mutashabihat comparison records after benchmark examples exist.

This order establishes trustworthy source text and provenance before adding increasingly interpretive layers.

docs.title: QuranKit Dataset Evaluation
docs.text:
Status: Initial research and integration assessment Last reviewed: 2026-11-14 Scope: Candidate datasets and services for the QuranKit research framework

This document is a technical due-diligence record, not legal advice. Re-check each source's current terms before every release or redistribution.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
QuranKit is intended to be a Python-first framework for reproducible Qur'anic research. Its datasets must be treated as independently governed research assets, not as interchangeable files bundled with the software.

This document evaluates candidate sources for:

  • Qur'anic Arabic text and structural metadata
  • Morphological and syntactic annotation
  • Lexical resources and classical dictionaries
  • Historical Arabic and Islamicate texts
  • Tafsir, translations, hadith, and other scholarly material
  • API-based content providers

The central rule is source-first data governance: every imported record must retain its source, edition or release, license/terms, retrieval date, attribution, and transformation history.

docs.title: Recommended initial path
docs.text:
1. Use Tanzil as the leading candidate for a baseline Qur'anic text edition and structural metadata, subject to strict preservation of the supplied text and attribution.
  2. Build QuranKit's own deterministic indexing, tokenization interfaces, search, concordance, comparison, and research-run infrastructure independently of third-party annotation.
  3. Treat Quranic Arabic Corpus (QAC) as an optional, separately licensed annotation provider. Do not modify or redistribute its annotation until its terms and the relationship between its download notice, GPL wording, and FAQ restrictions have been reviewed.
  4. Treat Quran Foundation as an optional API integration for end-user applications, not as a source for a redistributable QuranKit dataset unless a separate written license permits it.
  5. Use OpenITI in a later historical-text research extension. Do not assume that every text in the corpus has uniform provenance, fidelity, or reuse rights.
  6. Do not bundle classical dictionary content, translations, tafsir, audio, or hadith collections until rights are verified at the individual resource/edition level.

docs.title: Dataset strategy
docs.text: Layer Initial strategy Bundled by default? Quranic text Tanzil candidate; preserve source file exactly Only after release-specific validation Structural metadata Tanzil metadata candidate Only after terms and attribution are recorded Tokenization/indexes Generate from permitted source text using QuranKit code Yes, if output does not unlawfully reproduce restricted source material Morphology/syntax Native schema plus optional QAC adapter No QAC data by default Lexicons Provider adapters and user-supplied licensed packs No Tafsir/translations Edition-specific provider packs No Historical corpus OpenITI adapter / external corpus reference No API content Live provider integration No raw API data redistribution

docs.title: 3. Evaluation criteria
docs.text:
Each candidate should be assessed against the following criteria before adoption:

  1. Coverage — full Qur'an, selected surahs, selected books, or partial annotation.
  2. Edition identity — exact text edition, script, orthography, publisher, release number, and date.
  3. Accuracy and review — editorial process, scholarly review, known limitations, correction process.
  4. Annotation scope — morphology, syntax, roots, lemmas, senses, semantic relations, or metadata.
  5. License and terms — copying, modification, redistribution, commercial use, API use, caching, and derived data.
  6. Attribution — exact credit text, source links, citation format, and notice retention.
  7. Provenance — source chain for each record, not just the website from which it was downloaded.
  8. Technical suitability — machine-readable formats, stable identifiers, encoding, schema, and update mechanism.
  9. Offline suitability — whether local copies are permitted and how they must be refreshed.
  10. Research reproducibility — whether a result can cite an exact source release and transformation.

A source being publicly viewable or downloadable does not automatically mean that it is open-licensed or may be redistributed.

docs.title: 4.1 Tanzil Quran Text
docs.text:
Role: Candidate baseline Arabic text source.

Official pages:

  • Text license: https://tanzil.net/docs/Text_License
  • Download: https://tanzil.net/download/
  • Metadata: https://tanzil.net/docs/Quran_Metadata
  • Metadata updates: https://tanzil.net/docs/metadata_updates

What it provides

Tanzil distributes machine-readable Qur'anic text in multiple forms and formats. Its download page identifies version 1.1, published in February 2021. The metadata resource describes surah information and structural divisions including juz, hizb, hizb quarters, manzil, ruku, Medina Mushaf page numbers, and sajdah locations/types. It also includes revelation order and other surah-level fields.

License and use conditions observed

The Tanzil text license page states CC BY 3.0 and separately sets out specific terms:

  • Verbatim copies may be copied and distributed.
  • Changing the text is not allowed.
  • Use in websites and applications is permitted with clear source attribution and a link to Tanzil.
  • The copyright notice must accompany verbatim copies and be reproduced appropriately in files derived from or containing a substantial portion of the text.
  • Users should check updates and link to Tanzil so users can track changes.

The explicit no-change condition is important. QuranKit must not silently normalize, rewrite, strip marks from, or otherwise alter the canonical stored source text and then describe that altered copy as the original Tanzil text.

Assessment

  • Coverage: full Qur'an.
  • Technical suitability: high; machine-readable downloads and separate metadata.
  • Structural metadata: useful for navigation and research segmentation.
  • Accuracy: Tanzil describes the text as carefully produced, verified, and monitored. QuranKit should still perform independent integrity checks and retain source checksums.
  • Offline use: potentially suitable for a bundled source pack, subject to exact terms and preservation.
  • Main risk: confusing an analytical/search representation with a permitted modified copy of the source text.

Recommendation: ADOPT AS A CANDIDATE BASELINE, WITH STRICT SOURCE PRESERVATION.

Implementation requirements:

  1. Store the downloaded original bytes as an immutable source artifact.
  2. Record exact release/version, download URL, retrieval timestamp, SHA-256, and attribution notice.
  3. Preserve original ayah strings exactly in the source layer.
  4. Put normalized search strings in separately generated fields, never overwrite source text.
  5. Link visibly to Tanzil in documentation and any user-facing application using the data.
  6. Re-check the source's update page and terms before each dataset release.
  7. Keep the text and metadata as separately registered assets, each with its own provenance and license record.

docs.title: 4.2 Tanzil Quran Metadata
docs.text:
Role: Candidate structural metadata provider.

Official pages:

  • Metadata description: https://tanzil.net/docs/Quran_Metadata
  • Metadata change history: https://tanzil.net/docs/metadata_updates

The metadata page lists:

  • Surah number, ayah count, revelation order, start line, ruku count, and names
  • Juz
  • Hizb and hizb quarters
  • Manzil
  • Ruku
  • Medina Mushaf page
  • Sajdah location and type

The metadata change history identifies version 1.0 and a release date of 28 February 2008, with historical updates including revelation order, sajdah, ruku, and hizb-quarter information.

Assessment

This is highly useful for QuranKit's structural model. However, metadata should not be treated as timeless or universally edition-independent. Page numbers, for example, are tied to a particular Mushaf layout. Revelation order and other historical metadata may have scholarly conventions or disagreements.

Recommendation: ADOPT AS A VERSIONED METADATA PROVIDER, NOT AS UNQUALIFIED UNIVERSAL TRUTH.

Implementation requirements:

  • Store the provider's original field values and identifiers.
  • Label page numbers with the Mushaf/layout convention.
  • Preserve source/version and retrieval information.
  • Do not infer missing metadata.
  • Allow multiple providers or scholarly views for fields where disagreement exists.
  • Cite Tanzil as the source in generated metadata documentation.

docs.title: 4.3 Quranic Arabic Corpus (QAC)
docs.text:
Role: Optional morphology, syntax, and linguistic annotation provider.

Official pages:

  • Download: https://corpus.quran.com/download/
  • FAQ: https://corpus.quran.com/faq.jsp
  • License: https://corpus.quran.com/license.jsp

What it provides

The download page identifies version 0.4 of the morphological data and describes syntactic and morphological annotation of the Qur'an. It states that the corpus builds on verified Arabic text distributed by Tanzil. The site also provides word-by-word, dictionary, syntactic treebank, ontology, and grammar resources.

Terms requiring special care

The download page labels the data GNU General Public License and says:

  • Verbatim copies may be copied and distributed.
  • Changing the file is not allowed.
  • Use in websites or applications requires clear source attribution and a link to the corpus.
  • Copyright notices must be retained in verbatim copies and substantial derived works.

The FAQ separately says research data is made available for research purposes, should not be used commercially, and requires citation in research publications. It also notes that annotation is still undergoing correction.

These statements should not be collapsed into a simplistic claim that all QAC material is freely modifiable for all commercial purposes. The exact version, asset, license text, and any additional conditions need review. If commercial use is planned, obtain written clarification from the maintainers or legal review before integrating the data into a commercial distribution.

Assessment

  • Linguistic value: high.
  • Annotation scope: useful for morphology and syntax.
  • Maturity: valuable but the FAQ explicitly notes ongoing correction.
  • Technical suitability: promising, subject to schema mapping and stable token alignment.
  • Redistribution/modification: constrained and requires legal review.
  • Research quality: must preserve annotation as a sourced scholarly/computational layer, not an unquestionable ground truth.

Recommendation: SUPPORT THROUGH AN OPTIONAL ADAPTER; DO NOT MAKE IT A REQUIRED OR DEFAULT REDISTRIBUTED DATASET.

Implementation requirements:

  1. Preserve original downloaded files unchanged if local storage is permitted.
  2. Record version, checksum, citation, exact license text, and retrieval date.
  3. Map QAC records to QuranKit identifiers without rewriting the source annotation.
  4. Keep QuranKit's internal schema separate from the provider's schema.
  5. Do not publish modified QAC files as though they were official QAC data.
  6. Record annotation uncertainty and source corrections.
  7. Obtain written clarification before commercial distribution or transformation.

docs.title: 4.4 Quran Foundation APIs
docs.text:
Role: Optional live API integration for applications.

Official pages:

  • Developer terms: https://api-docs.quran.com/legal/developer-terms/
  • FAQ: https://api-docs.quran.foundation/docs/tutorials/faq/

What it provides

Quran Foundation's APIs cover Quran text, translations, metadata, audio, reflections, and other content. This can be useful for application developers who need provider-managed access and content synchronization.

Terms observed

The developer terms, last updated 11 October 2026 on the page reviewed, distinguish between displaying content to end users and redistributing raw content as data.

The terms permit qualifying applications to charge for subscriptions, in-app purchases, advertising, donations, or freemium access, provided the content is displayed within the application experience and the other terms are followed.

They restrict selling, sublicensing, or redistributing QF content/raw API data. A separate signed commercial license is required before distributing it as a dataset, feed, API, download, or content package. The terms also specify caching limits and require Content Sync APIs as the permitted path for maintaining certain offline copies.

Assessment

  • Application integration: useful.
  • Dataset mirroring: not an assumed permitted use.
  • Offline behavior: must follow the exact Content Sync rules.
  • Redistribution: requires separate permission where specified.
  • Long-term reproducibility: API content can change; store provider identifiers and retrieval metadata where permitted.

Recommendation: OPTIONAL API CONNECTOR ONLY. DO NOT USE AS THE DEFAULT SOURCE FOR A REDISTRIBUTABLE DATA PACK.

Implementation requirements:

  • Make API use opt-in and provider-specific.
  • Follow rate limits, caching limits, privacy requirements, and Content Sync rules.
  • Never scrape or bulk-extract outside authorized API responses.
  • Do not expose raw QF data through QuranKit's own dataset downloads or API unless separately licensed.
  • Clearly label provider content in results.
  • Keep API credentials outside source control.
  • Do not assume all QF content assets share identical rights.

docs.title: 4.5 OpenITI Corpus
docs.text:
Role: Later historical Arabic and Islamicate text research extension.

Official pages:

  • Corpus overview: https://openiti.org/projects/OpenITI%20Corpus.html
  • Terms of use: https://openiti.org/docs/Terms%20of%20Use.html
  • Documentation: https://openiti.org/documentation/
  • Releases: https://github.com/OpenITI/RELEASE

What it provides

OpenITI is a machine-actionable collection of Arabic and Persian Islamicate texts. It can support historical language research, text reuse, source comparison, author/book metadata, and broader context around scholarly works.

License and quality considerations

OpenITI documentation describes corpus releases under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The currently surfaced terms page also describes non-commercial Creative Material under CC BY-SA wording and distinguishes third-party material. These pages and the applicable release/contributor terms must be reconciled for the exact item being used. Do not assume one license covers every text, scan, image, edition, or third-party component in the ecosystem.

OpenITI itself notes that its texts come from different sources and have varying fidelity to print editions, including manual transcription and OCR errors. Its documentation recommends citing individual file URIs and the relevant release.

Assessment

  • Research value: high for historical context and text reuse.
  • Direct Quran text authority: not appropriate as the canonical Qur'an source.
  • Quality: heterogeneous; each text requires source-level evaluation.
  • License: non-commercial and share-alike constraints make it unsuitable for an assumed unrestricted commercial dataset.
  • Technical suitability: strong potential for a later adapter.

Recommendation: LATER OPTIONAL HISTORICAL-CORPUS CONNECTOR; NOT PART OF THE CORE MVP.

Implementation requirements:

  • Identify the exact OpenITI release and file URI.
  • Retain edition and source metadata.
  • Check the applicable license for each asset and any third-party content.
  • Preserve OCR/transcription quality warnings.
  • Do not imply that corpus inclusion means scholarly verification.
  • Keep this data outside the core Quran text package.

docs.title: 4.6 Classical Arabic dictionaries and lexical resources
docs.text:
Role: Root, lemma, lexical sense, definition, and historical usage research.

A relevant candidate identified in the initial survey is the Linguistic Data Consortium's Classical Arabic Dictionary (LDC2021L01):

  • Catalog: https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2021L01

The catalog describes a large collection of Arabic material from texts dating between 431 and 1104 CE, including word occurrences, source documents, and metadata. It is distributed under an LDC User Agreement, with access and fees depending on membership.

Assessment

This resource may be valuable for historical lexical research, but it is not a freely redistributable dictionary pack. Access is governed by the LDC agreement. It also represents a corpus-derived resource rather than a simple replacement for individual classical lexicons.

For named classical works (for example, Lisān al-ʿArab, Maqāyīs al-Lughah, al-Mufradāt, or al-Ṣiḥāḥ), QuranKit must distinguish:

  • The public-domain status of an old authored work, where applicable
  • Copyright in a modern edited edition, introduction, notes, and critical apparatus
  • Copyright and terms of a digital transcription or database
  • The source and reliability of any extracted lexical records

Recommendation: BUILD A PROVIDER-NEUTRAL LEXICON SCHEMA FIRST. ADD ONLY RESOURCE PACKS WITH VERIFIED ITEM-LEVEL RIGHTS.

Do not scrape online dictionary websites or copy modern editions merely because the underlying classical author died centuries ago.

docs.title: 4.7 Translations and tafsir
docs.text:
Role: Contextual interpretation, comparative translation, and scholarly commentary.

No general blanket license should be assumed for translations or tafsir. A translation is an authored work; a modern edition of a classical tafsir may include editorial material, notes, and other protected contributions. A provider's API permission may also differ from permission to redistribute a local data package.

Recommendation: KEEP THESE AS SEPARATE EDITION-SPECIFIC PLUGINS.

For every translation or tafsir edition, record:

  • Original title and language
  • Author/translator and editor
  • Publisher and edition
  • Publication date
  • Source URL or catalog identifier
  • Exact license or written permission
  • Allowed use: display, research, commercial, offline, modification, redistribution
  • Required attribution
  • Whether excerpts or derived indexes are permitted

Do not merge translation or tafsir text into the canonical Arabic text record.

docs.title: 4.8 Hadith collections and scholarly works
docs.text:
Role: Later research linking ayahs to narrations, explanations, and scholarly discussions.

A hadith work may be old while a modern edition, translation, numbering system, grading, commentary, or database is not. Numbering can differ by edition and publisher. Online accessibility does not establish permission to download, transform, or redistribute.

Recommendation: DEFER DATA INGESTION. DESIGN THE SOURCE AND CITATION MODEL NOW.

Each record should identify the collection, book/chapter, hadith number as used by a named edition, edition/publisher, narrator chain where available, grading source, and exact citation locator. Do not combine variant numbering systems into one supposedly universal ID.

docs.title: 5. Source comparison matrix
docs.text: Source Primary value Coverage Rights posture observed MVP decision Tanzil text Arabic Qur'an text Full Qur'an Verbatim distribution; no text changes; attribution/link Candidate baseline Tanzil metadata Surah and structural metadata Full Qur'an structure Source attribution; verify metadata-specific terms Candidate baseline QAC Morphology and syntax Qur'an annotation GPL wording plus FAQ non-commercial research limitation; no changes stated Optional adapter; legal review Quran Foundation API content and sync Broad API content Display permitted under conditions; raw redistribution requires separate license Optional API connector OpenITI Historical Arabic/Persian corpus Large, heterogeneous corpus Non-commercial/share-alike terms; check item-level third-party rights Later extension LDC Classical Arabic Dictionary Historical Arabic corpus/lexical data Large historical corpus LDC agreement and access terms Optional licensed provider Translation/tafsir editions Interpretation and translation Edition-specific Must verify per edition Later plugins Hadith datasets Narrations and references Collection-specific Must verify per edition/database Later plugins

docs.title: 6. QuranKit data governance requirements
docs.text:
Every source asset must have a manifest. Suggested fields:

dataset_id: tanzil.quran_text.uthmani
provider: Tanzil Project
asset_name: Quran Text - Uthmani
version: "1.1"
release_date: "2021-02"
retrieved_at: "YYYY-MM-DD"
source_url: "https://tanzil.net/download/"
license_name: "CC BY 3.0 (with source-specific terms)"
license_url: "https://tanzil.net/docs/Text_License"
redistribution: "verbatim_only"
modification: false
commercial_use: "verify_scope_and_terms"
attribution_required: true
attribution_text: "Tanzil Quran Text — Tanzil Project — https://tanzil.net"
source_checksum_sha256: "<computed-at-ingestion>"
format: "provider-original-format"
language: "ar"
script: "uthmani"
notes:
  - "Keep original source bytes unchanged."
  - "Generated search forms are separate derived fields."

The example is illustrative. The ingestion pipeline must fill in actual retrieval dates, checksums, format, and exact attribution text from the downloaded source. Never ship placeholder values in a released manifest.

docs.title: Required provenance fields
docs.text:
At minimum, each dataset and record should be traceable to:

  • provider_id
  • dataset_id
  • dataset_version
  • source_record_id
  • source_uri
  • license_id
  • retrieved_at
  • source_checksum
  • ingestion_pipeline_version
  • transformation_id
  • review_status

For scholarly annotations, add:

  • annotator/author
  • editor/reviewer
  • edition
  • method
  • confidence or uncertainty, if supplied
  • correction history
  • disagreement/variant information

docs.title: Separation of layers
docs.text:
QuranKit should keep the following distinct:

  1. Source artifact — the exact downloaded file, preserved when permitted.
  2. Canonical source record — structured representation linked to the source artifact.
  3. Derived index — search normalization, token lookup, FTS index, embeddings, and other generated structures.
  4. Scholarly annotation — sourced morphology, syntax, lexical, semantic, or interpretive statements.
  5. Research result — output of a reproducible algorithm with its inputs and method.
  6. User annotation — a user's own notes, hypotheses, and corrections.

A derived index must never be presented as if it were the original source text or the source provider's official annotation.

docs.title: 7. Dataset ingestion and release workflow
docs.text:
Recommended lifecycle:

  1. Discover — identify the provider and exact asset.
  2. Review rights — record license, terms, attribution, redistribution, modification, commercial use, and caching conditions.
  3. Acquire — use the official download or authorized API.
  4. Freeze source — preserve original bytes if permitted; compute SHA-256.
  5. Validate — check encoding, record counts, identifiers, expected coverage, and schema.
  6. Map — map provider identifiers into QuranKit identifiers without discarding provider IDs.
  7. Transform — produce derived indexes in a separate, versioned pipeline.
  8. Review — run integrity tests and, for scholarly annotation, expert review where possible.
  9. Package — include manifests, notices, citations, and checksums.
  10. Publish — publish code and data as separate artifacts with separate licenses.
  11. Monitor — track source updates, corrections, and license changes.

If a source prohibits modification, do not modify the source artifact. If a source prohibits redistribution, do not put its data into a downloadable package. If terms are ambiguous, pause publication and seek clarification.

docs.title: Text integrity
docs.text:
• Verify surah count and expected ayah counts against the chosen edition.
  • Verify stable surah/ayah identifiers.
  • Compare the imported source against the original source artifact.
  • Ensure Unicode normalization never overwrites the source string.
  • Keep Uthmani and Imlai editions distinct.
  • Detect missing, duplicated, reordered, or unexpectedly altered ayahs.
  • Record all validation results in a machine-readable report.

docs.title: Metadata integrity
docs.text:
• Validate all surah references.
  • Validate Juz/hizb/ruku/page ranges.
  • Label page numbering by Mushaf convention.
  • Preserve provider values and do not fill gaps by guessing.
  • Allow multiple sourced values when scholarly conventions differ.

docs.title: Linguistic annotation integrity
docs.text:
• Validate token alignment against the exact text edition used by the annotation.
  • Do not assume one provider's tokenization matches another's.
  • Keep morphological segmentation separate from orthographic word tokens.
  • Preserve provider labels and original annotation IDs.
  • Track annotation corrections and unresolved ambiguity.
  • Do not infer roots or lemmas from string similarity alone.

docs.title: Licensing integrity
docs.text:
• Ensure each packaged asset has a manifest and notice.
  • Fail release checks if an asset has unknown rights status.
  • Prevent restricted assets from entering public data packages.
  • Verify all required attribution links and license copies.
  • Keep third-party assets separate from QuranKit's own code license.

docs.title: 9. Proposed package layout
docs.text:
qurankit/
├── src/
│   └── qurankit/
│       ├── datasets/
│       │   ├── manifest.py
│       │   ├── registry.py
│       │   ├── provenance.py
│       │   └── validation.py
│       ├── providers/
│       │   ├── tanzil/
│       │   ├── qac/
│       │   ├── quran_foundation/
│       │   ├── openiti/
│       │   └── lexicons/
│       └── ...
├── data/
│   └── manifests/
│       ├── tanzil-quran-text.yaml
│       └── tanzil-quran-metadata.yaml
├── licenses/
│   └── third_party/
├── docs/
│   ├── data-model.md
│   ├── arabic-text-standard.md
│   └── datasets.md
└── tests/
