The actual third-party data files should be stored separately from source code wherever licensing, repository size, or release cadence makes that preferable.

docs.title: Phase A — source governance (first)
docs.text:
• Implement DatasetManifest.
  • Implement a dataset registry.
  • Implement SHA-256 and source artifact metadata.
  • Implement license/rights status values: approved, restricted, permission_required, unknown, rejected.
  • Make release packaging fail for unknown or permission_required assets.

docs.title: Phase B — text and metadata baseline
docs.text:
• Evaluate and ingest Tanzil text under its exact terms.
  • Evaluate and ingest Tanzil metadata.
  • Preserve original source artifacts.
  • Generate independent QuranKit indexes and structural records.
  • Add ayah count, ordering, and checksum tests.

docs.title: Phase C — linguistic adapters
docs.text:
• Define provider-neutral morphology and syntax schemas.
  • Prototype QAC mapping in a local, non-redistributed development environment if permitted.
  • Resolve the QAC license/FAQ ambiguity before publishing any integrated data.
  • Add adapter conformance tests.

docs.title: Phase D — research extensions
docs.text:
• Add lexicon provider interfaces.
  • Add edition-specific translation and tafsir providers.
  • Add OpenITI historical-text adapter.
  • Add hadith and scholarly-reference models.
  • Review every source independently.

docs.title: 11. Open questions before the first public data release
docs.text:
1. Which exact Tanzil text form should be the default: Uthmani, simple, or another offered form?
  2. Will QuranKit distribute a Tanzil-derived data pack, or require users to download it directly?
  3. Does the intended distribution include commercial use?
  4. Can QAC maintainers clarify in writing the scope of the GPL statement, no-change clause, and non-commercial FAQ?
  5. Which lexicon edition(s) can be legally redistributed in structured form?
  6. Which translation/tafsir editions have explicit licenses?
  7. Which Mushaf convention should be used for page metadata?
  8. How should QuranKit represent disagreements in revelation-order, Makki/Madani, and other scholarly metadata?

docs.title: 12. Source references
docs.text:
Primary sources reviewed for this initial assessment:

  • Tanzil Text License — https://tanzil.net/docs/Text_License
  • Tanzil Download — https://tanzil.net/download/
  • Tanzil Quran Metadata — https://tanzil.net/docs/Quran_Metadata
  • Tanzil Metadata Updates — https://tanzil.net/docs/metadata_updates
  • Quranic Arabic Corpus Download — https://corpus.quran.com/download/
  • Quranic Arabic Corpus FAQ — https://corpus.quran.com/faq.jsp
  • Quranic Arabic Corpus License — https://corpus.quran.com/license.jsp
  • Quran Foundation Developer Terms — https://api-docs.quran.com/legal/developer-terms/
  • Quran Foundation FAQ — https://api-docs.quran.foundation/docs/tutorials/faq/
  • OpenITI Corpus — https://openiti.org/projects/OpenITI%20Corpus.html
  • OpenITI Terms of Use — https://openiti.org/docs/Terms%20of%20Use.html
  • OpenITI Documentation — https://openiti.org/documentation/
  • OpenITI Releases — https://github.com/OpenITI/RELEASE
  • LDC Classical Arabic Dictionary — https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2021L01

docs.title: 13. Final position
docs.text:
QuranKit should not aim to own or repackage every available Islamic text resource. It should provide a trustworthy framework for connecting, validating, indexing, comparing, and citing sources under their actual terms.

The strongest initial architecture is:

  • a carefully sourced Qur'anic text layer;
  • a versioned structural metadata layer;
  • a provider-neutral linguistic annotation layer;
  • a provenance and licensing registry;
  • deterministic Python research tools;
  • optional adapters for external scholarly resources.

This approach keeps QuranKit useful to researchers and AI agents without confusing computational convenience with textual authority, scholarly consensus, or permission to redistribute data.

docs.title: Quran Research Engine --- Project Plan
docs.text: Status: Initial project specification\ Document version: 0.1.0\ Scope: Text-first computational Qur'anic research framework

docs.title: 1. Vision
docs.text:
Build a modular, Python-first, open-source framework for systematically retrieving, exploring, comparing, and analyzing the Qur'anic text and its linguistic and structural features.

The framework should serve:

  • Researchers working with Qur'anic text and Arabic language data.
  • Developers building research applications.
  • Educators and students conducting structured textual exploration.
  • AI agents that need reliable, traceable research tools.

The initial product is a reusable Python library. MCP, REST APIs, command-line tools, notebooks, and user-facing applications are interfaces built on top of the same core functionality.

docs.title: 2. Product principles
docs.text:
1. Text-first, expandable: Start with Qur'anic text, lexical resources, morphology, grammar, semantics, and textual relationships. Design extension points for tafsir, hadith, and other scholarly resources without requiring them in the MVP.
  2. Source traceability: Every imported annotation or dataset must retain source, version, license, and attribution metadata.
  3. Preserve originals: Never overwrite source text with normalized or transformed text.
  4. Separate evidence from inference: Distinguish source-provided annotations, deterministic computational results, model-generated suggestions, and scholarly interpretation.
  5. Reproducibility: Record dataset versions, algorithm versions, parameters, and normalization profiles used for a result.
  6. Offline-capable: Core research workflows should work without a hosted service after the required datasets are installed.
  7. Provider-neutral: The core library must not depend on a particular LLM, MCP client, cloud provider, or external API.
  8. Modular dependencies: Keep optional NLP, vector-search, graph, API, and agent dependencies out of the minimal installation.

docs.title: Qur'anic text and structure
docs.text:
• Canonical surah and ayah identifiers.
  • Source-preserving Arabic text storage.
  • Uthmani and Imlai representations where licensed and available.
  • Word-level segmentation and stable word identifiers.
  • Surah, ayah, juz, hizb, rubu', page, and other structural metadata when sourced.
  • Text and dataset validation.

docs.title: Arabic text processing
docs.text:
• Unicode normalization.
  • Configurable search normalization profiles.
  • Diacritic-aware and diacritic-insensitive search.
  • Explicit handling of hamza, alif variants, alif maqsurah, ta marbutah, Quranic annotation marks, and pause signs.
  • Exact, phrase, token, prefix, and fuzzy search.
  • Reversible or inspectable normalization mappings where practical.

docs.title: Lexicon and Qur'anic vocabulary
docs.text:
• Root and lemma lookup when supported by sourced annotations.
  • Dictionary entries from separately licensed sources.
  • Arabic definitions and source-language text.
  • Derivatives and morphological forms.
  • Synonym, antonym, and semantic relations only when attributed to a source or clearly marked as computational suggestions.
  • Qur'anic occurrence lists and contextual concordance.
  • Support for Qur'anic vocabulary resources such as Al-Mufradat where lawful digital data is available.

docs.title: Morphology and grammar
docs.text:
• Word-level morphological annotations.
  • Part of speech, lemma, root, and inflectional features where sourced.
  • Nahwu and i'rab annotations where reliable data is available.
  • Sarf and derivational relationships.
  • Annotation provenance and uncertainty.
  • No unsupported automatic assertion of a root or grammatical analysis.

docs.title: Semantic and thematic exploration
docs.text:
• Contextual concordance.
  • Word co-occurrence and collocation.
  • Semantic-field exploration.
  • Related-word and concept links with explicit provenance.
  • Wujuh wa nazair research support, preserving the cited scholarly source.
  • Optional semantic search as a discovery aid, never as a replacement for exact search.

docs.title: Textual relationships and mutashabihat
docs.text:
• Exact repeated phrase detection.
  • Near-duplicate phrase detection.
  • Similar ayah and passage discovery.
  • Word-order and lexical variation comparison.
  • Shared-root and shared-lemma analysis.
  • Similar openings, endings, and recurring expressions.
  • Results classified by method and confidence; similarity must not be presented as proof of interpretive equivalence.

docs.title: Computational analysis
docs.text:
• Letter, word, lemma, and root frequency.
  • Ayah and surah length statistics.
  • Distribution and co-occurrence analysis.
  • Reproducible statistical experiments.
  • Exportable result tables and machine-readable outputs.

docs.title: Research interface foundations
docs.text:
• Stable Python API.
  • CLI for common retrieval and dataset-management tasks.
  • Jupyter-friendly result objects and examples.
  • Optional MCP server exposing selected read-only research tools.

docs.title: 3.2 Designed for later extensions
docs.text:
These are not MVP requirements, but the data model and package boundaries should permit them:

  • Tafsir corpora and comparative tafsir research.
  • Hadith collections, takhrij, isnad, narrator data, and grading opinions.
  • Scholar biographies, works, and attributed scholarly positions.
  • Ulum al-Qur'an resources, asbab al-nuzul, Makki/Madani studies, and nasikh-mansukh research.
  • Qira'at and their textual/phonetic annotations.
  • Tajwid, waqf, and ibtida'.
  • Fiqh and usul al-fiqh research.
  • Seerah and historical source integration.
  • Memorization, muraja'ah, and Hifz applications.
  • Web-based research explorer and hosted API.

docs.title: 3.3 Non-goals for the MVP
docs.text:
• Producing autonomous religious rulings or fatwas.
  • Replacing tafsir, qualified scholarship, or human review.
  • Treating numerical patterns as proof of theological claims.
  • Generating unsourced interpretations.
  • Bundling copyrighted dictionaries, translations, or corpora without redistribution rights.
  • Requiring cloud access or an LLM for core functionality.

docs.title: 4. Research result categories
docs.text:
Every result should identify what kind of claim it represents.

Category Meaning Example

Source text Text reproduced from an An ayah in a named text identified source edition

Source annotation Annotation supplied by A morphology tag from a a corpus or scholar cited corpus

Deterministic result Reproducible output Exact phrase match from a defined algorithm

Computational Candidate requiring Fuzzy semantic suggestion validation similarity

Scholarly A position attributed A dictionary or tafsir interpretation to a named work or explanation scholar

Research hypothesis A proposed pattern or A possible structural relationship correspondence

Do not collapse these categories into one unqualified answer.

docs.title: 5.1 Core entities
docs.text:
Initial logical entities:

  • TextEdition
  • Surah
  • Ayah
  • WordToken
  • WordSegment (optional, for sub-word segmentation)
  • Dataset
  • Source
  • SourceEdition
  • Annotation
  • LexicalEntry
  • Root
  • Lemma
  • MorphologicalAnalysis
  • GrammarAnalysis
  • SemanticRelation
  • Occurrence
  • ResearchResult
  • AlgorithmVersion

docs.title: 5.2 Identifier strategy
docs.text:
• Use stable Qur'anic references such as 2:255 for surah:ayah.
  • Give each word token a stable identifier tied to the text edition and tokenization version.
  • Do not assume token indices are interchangeable across editions or tokenization schemes.
  • Preserve source identifiers when importing external corpora.
  • Record mappings between identifiers rather than silently replacing them.

docs.title: 5.3 Provenance fields
docs.text:
Imported data should, where available, include:

  • Source title and creator/author.
  • Source URL or persistent identifier.
  • Edition, publisher, publication year, volume, page, or entry.
  • Dataset release and retrieval date.
  • License and permitted uses.
  • Original source identifier.
  • Importer and transformation version.
  • Verification status and reviewer notes.

Missing bibliographic fields must remain explicitly unknown; do not invent them.

docs.title: 5.4 Suggested storage strategy
docs.text:
Start simple:

  • SQLite for local structured data and metadata.
  • SQLite FTS5 for initial full-text search.
  • JSONL or Parquet for portable dataset exports where appropriate.
  • NetworkX for early graph exploration.
  • Optional vector index for semantic discovery.

Add PostgreSQL, a dedicated graph database, or external search infrastructure only when demonstrated scale or collaboration needs justify them.

docs.title: 6. Arabic text and normalization policy
docs.text:
Store original source text unchanged. Derived forms must be separate fields or generated views.

Provide named normalization profiles, for example:

  • exact_source: exact comparison against the selected source representation.
  • diacritics_insensitive: removes specified diacritics while retaining other distinctions.
  • search: applies a documented set of search-oriented equivalences.
  • uthmani_to_search: maps selected Uthmani signs for search while preserving the original.
  • custom: user-specified normalization rules.

Normalization must be explicit in every search and comparison result. Do not use one universal normalized form for every research task.

Test Unicode behavior, combining marks, Quranic annotation signs, hamza forms, alif variants, alif maqsurah, ta marbutah, and pause marks.

docs.title: 7. Dataset strategy and licensing
docs.text:
Use source adapters rather than hard-coding one provider.

Candidate resources to evaluate include:

  • Quranic Arabic Corpus for word-level morphology and syntactic annotations.
  • Quran Foundation resources and APIs for Qur'anic text and related data.
  • OpenITI for classical Arabic textual resources.
  • CAMeL Tools and other Arabic NLP projects for optional general Arabic processing.
  • Digitized classical dictionaries and Qur'anic vocabulary works, subject to source and edition verification.

Evaluation checklist for each candidate:

  1. Is the source authoritative and suitable for the intended task?
  2. What exact edition or dataset release is provided?
  3. Is the Arabic text complete and correctly encoded?
  4. Are annotations human-authored, automatically generated, or mixed?
  5. Is the license compatible with use, modification, and redistribution?
  6. Can attribution and source references be preserved?
  7. Can the data be versioned and checksummed?
  8. Is there a known quality-control or correction process?

Do not infer redistribution permission from public web availability. When rights are unclear, provide an adapter or user-supplied import workflow instead of bundling the data.

docs.title: 8. Package and repository architecture
docs.text:
Proposed initial repository:

quran-research/
├── README.md
├── LICENSE
├── pyproject.toml
├── plan.md
├── AGENTS.md
├── docs/
│   ├── architecture.md
│   ├── data-model.md
│   ├── datasets.md
│   ├── arabic-text-standard.md
│   ├── research-methodology.md
│   └── distribution.md
├── src/
│   └── quran_research/
│       ├── core/
│       ├── text/
│       ├── lexicon/
│       ├── morphology/
│       ├── syntax/
│       ├── semantics/
│       ├── search/
│       ├── mutashabihat/
│       ├── analysis/
│       ├── datasets/
│       └── cli/
├── tests/
│   ├── unit/
│   ├── integration/
│   ├── fixtures/
│   └── golden/
├── examples/
├── benchmarks/
└── .github/
    └── workflows/

Keep MCP and API integrations optional. They may live in optional extras initially and be split into separate distributions only when independent release cycles or dependencies make that worthwhile.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The Python library is the source of truth for research functionality. Example API sketches:

from quran_research import Quran

quran = Quran()

ayah = quran.ayah("2:255")
results = quran.search.phrase("...")
occurrences = quran.lexicon.occurrences(root="...")
matches = quran.mutashabihat.find("2:48")
comparison = quran.compare("2:48", "2:123")

These are design examples, not a commitment to final signatures. Final APIs must be consistent, typed, documented, and tested.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Provide commands for dataset inspection, installation, validation, and basic search. Example sketches:

quran-research data list
quran-research data install core
quran-research data validate core
quran-research search phrase "..."

docs.title: MCP and function calling
docs.text: Expose a small set of well-defined, read-only tools after the underlying Python functions are stable. Tool descriptions must explain input formats, normalization, dataset requirements, and result provenance.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: Defer until a real web or multi-user application requires it. Do not make the core library depend on a running API.

docs.title: Source hosting
docs.text:
• Host the canonical repository on GitHub.
  • Use issues and pull requests for contributions and review.
  • Use tags and release notes for versioned releases.
  • Use GitHub Actions for tests, linting, package builds, and release workflows.

docs.title: Python distribution
docs.text:
• Publish the core package to PyPI.
  • Use modern build metadata in pyproject.toml.
  • Prefer PyPI Trusted Publishing from GitHub Actions rather than long-lived publishing tokens.
  • Follow semantic versioning once the public API stabilizes.
  • Keep optional dependencies in extras, for example quran-research[api] or quran-research[mcp].

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Maintain versioned user and developer documentation.
  • Start with Markdown documentation in the repository.
  • Publish with Read the Docs or GitHub Pages when useful.
  • Include installation, quick start, dataset setup, API reference, source attribution, and reproducibility guidance.

docs.title: Dataset hosting
docs.text:
• Keep small manifests and metadata in Git.
  • Store larger redistributable datasets on an appropriate versioned data host such as Hugging Face Hub or Zenodo, subject to license.
  • For each release, publish a manifest containing source, version, license, checksum, and schema.
  • Support local dataset caches and offline use.
  • Avoid making the package installation download large datasets implicitly.

docs.title: Future hosted services
docs.text: A hosted REST API, web explorer, or managed MCP endpoint is a later product decision. The initial library should not require paid infrastructure.

docs.title: Text integrity
docs.text:
• Verify expected surah and ayah counts against the selected edition's documented specification.
  • Validate references and ordering.
  • Detect missing, duplicate, or malformed records.
  • Compare imported text against trusted source checksums or reference fixtures where available.

docs.title: Arabic processing
docs.text:
• Test Unicode normalization and combining marks.
  • Test diacritic-sensitive and insensitive search separately.
  • Test Uthmani/Imlai mapping without destroying original text.
  • Include edge cases for hamza, alif variants, ta marbutah, alif maqsurah, and Quranic marks.

docs.title: Lexicon and morphology
docs.text:
• Use reviewed examples with source references.
  • Test ambiguous roots and forms.
  • Preserve multiple analyses when the source supports them.
  • Do not claim complete lexical or grammatical coverage unless demonstrated.

docs.title: Search and mutashabihat
docs.text:
• Create gold-standard exact-match tests.
  • Evaluate fuzzy matching against reviewed examples.
  • Report the method and parameters used.
  • Measure false positives as well as recall.
  • Keep semantic similarity separate from scholarly equivalence.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
• Record dataset and algorithm versions.
  • Ensure deterministic algorithms produce stable outputs.
  • Test serialization and export.
  • Include end-to-end examples that can run offline.

docs.title: Phase 0 --- Repository and standards
docs.text:
• Create repository and packaging skeleton.
  • Finalize identifiers and core data models.
  • Write Arabic text and normalization standard.
  • Establish provenance and licensing manifest formats.
  • Select initial source datasets after review.

Exit criteria: A documented schema and a minimal package that installs and passes CI.

docs.title: Phase 1 --- Qur'anic core
docs.text:
• Load a verified, licensed text edition.
  • Implement surah/ayah retrieval.
  • Implement word token records and structural metadata.
  • Implement text validation and local storage.

Exit criteria: Reliable retrieval and integrity tests for the chosen edition.

docs.title: Phase 2 --- Search and lexical layer
docs.text:
• Implement normalization profiles.
  • Add exact, phrase, token, and occurrence search.
  • Add dictionary adapter interface.
  • Import one suitable lexical dataset if licensing and quality permit.
  • Add root and lemma lookup from a reviewed annotation source.

Exit criteria: Search results preserve original text and identify their data source.

docs.title: Phase 3 --- Linguistic analysis
docs.text:
• Add morphology and grammatical annotation adapters.
  • Add word-level and ayah-level analysis.
  • Preserve ambiguity and source attribution.

Exit criteria: Reviewed test cases demonstrate correct handling of supported annotations.

docs.title: Phase 4 --- Mutashabihat and computational research
docs.text:
• Implement exact repeated phrase detection.
  • Add configurable similarity methods.
  • Add comparison reports and statistical tools.
  • Build benchmark and reviewed evaluation sets.

Exit criteria: Results are reproducible and clearly classified by method.

docs.title: Phase 5 --- Developer and agent interfaces
docs.text:
• Stabilize Python SDK.
  • Add CLI and notebook examples.
  • Add optional MCP tools.
  • Consider REST API only if needed.

Exit criteria: A researcher and an agent can use the same tested core operations.

docs.title: Phase 6 --- Extensions
docs.text:
• Add optional tafsir and hadith adapters.
  • Add qira'at, tajwid, waqf, and other scholarly datasets.
  • Add Hifz applications and a research explorer as separate consumers.

Exit criteria: Extensions do not compromise core independence or provenance rules.

docs.title: 13. Initial release acceptance criteria
docs.text:
The first usable alpha should:

  • Install in a clean supported Python environment.
  • Load a documented and licensed Qur'anic text dataset.
  • Retrieve surahs, ayat, and word tokens by stable references.
  • Preserve source text and expose explicit normalization.
  • Perform exact and phrase search.
  • Expose dataset provenance and version metadata.
  • Include tests, examples, and basic documentation.
  • Work offline after data installation.
  • Avoid requiring an LLM, MCP server, or hosted database.

docs.title: 14. Open decisions
docs.text:
Do not silently settle these during implementation:

  • Which Qur'anic text edition(s) are included in the first release?
  • Which word segmentation convention and source identifiers are adopted?
  • Which lexical dataset can legally and technically be redistributed?
  • Which morphology and i'rab annotations are reliable enough to support?
  • Which Python versions are officially supported?
  • Which license is selected for original code?
  • Whether datasets are downloaded separately or distributed as optional packages.

Record the rationale for each decision in the relevant documentation.

docs.title: Arabic Text Processing
docs.text: QuranKit implements explicit, documented Arabic text processing following the Arabic Text Standard.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Source text is never modified — Original Arabic text is preserved exactly
  2. Normalized text is separate — Search/analysis uses derived normalized forms
  3. Normalization is explicit — Every operation documents its profile
  4. Mappings are preserved — Offsets between original and normalized text are tracked
  5. Unicode-aware — All processing uses proper Unicode handling

docs.title: Normalization Profiles
docs.text: QuranKit provides four built-in normalization profiles:

docs.title: 1. Exact Source (exact)
docs.text:
No normalization. Compares raw source text.

results = quran.search("بِسْمِ اللَّهِ", mode="exact")

docs.title: 2. Canonical Unicode (canonical)
docs.text:
Applies Unicode NFC normalization only.

results = quran.search("بِسْمِ اللَّهِ", mode="canonical")

docs.title: 3. Diacritic-Insensitive (diacritic_insensitive)
docs.text:
Removes harakat (short vowels) but keeps: - Quranic annotation signs (verse markers, sajdah marks) - Pause marks (waqf signs) - Shadda (gemination)

results = quran.search("بسم الله", mode="diacritic_insensitive")
# Matches: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ

docs.title: 4. Broad Search (broad)
docs.text:
Most permissive. Applies: - All diacritic-insensitive changes - Hamza normalization: أ إ آ ا → ا - Alif maqsurah: ى → ي - Ta marbutah: ة → ه - Removes tatweel (kashida): ـ - Removes Quranic annotation signs - Removes pause marks

results = quran.search("بسم الله", mode="broad")
# Matches all orthographic variants

docs.title: Using Normalization Directly
docs.text:
from qurankit.search import NormalizationEngine, NormalizationProfile

engine = NormalizationEngine()

# Get profile by name
profile = engine.get_profile("broad")

# Normalize text
text = "بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ"
normalized = profile.normalize(text)
print(normalized)  # "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم"

# Get character mappings
mappings = profile.normalize_with_mappings(text)
for mapping in mappings:
    print(f"Original: {mapping.original_char} -> Normalized: {mapping.normalized_char}")
    print(f"  Position: {mapping.original_pos} -> {mapping.normalized_pos}")

docs.title: Custom Normalization Profiles
docs.text:
from qurankit.search.normalization import NormalizationProfile, NormalizationRule

# Create custom profile
custom = NormalizationProfile(
    name="custom",
    rules=[
        NormalizationRule.remove_diacritics(keep_shadda=True),
        NormalizationRule.normalize_hamza(),
        NormalizationRule.normalize_ya_maqsurah(),
        NormalizationRule.normalize_ta_marbutah(),
        NormalizationRule.remove_tatweel(),
        NormalizationRule.remove_quranic_marks(),
        NormalizationRule.remove_pause_marks(),
    ]
)

# Register and use
engine.register_profile(custom)
results = quran.search("الرحمن", mode="custom")

docs.title: Hamza Variants
docs.text: Character Name Broad Normalization ا Alif ا أ Alif with Hamza Above ا إ Alif with Hamza Below ا آ Alif with Madda ا ؤ Waw with Hamza و ئ Ya with Hamza ي

docs.title: Alif Variants
docs.text: Character Name Broad Normalization ا Alif ا ٱ Alif Wasla ا آ Alif with Madda ا

docs.title: Alif Maqsurah
docs.text: Character Name Broad Normalization ى Alif Maqsurah ي ي Ya ي

docs.title: Ta Marbutah
docs.text: Character Name Broad Normalization ة Ta Marbutah ه ه Ha ه

docs.title: Quranic Marks (Preserved in Diacritic-Insensitive)
docs.text: Character Name Diacritic-Insensitive Broad ۝ Verse End Kept Removed ۩ Sajdah Kept Removed ۞ Ruku Kept Removed ۝ Quarter Hizb Kept Removed

docs.title: Pause Marks (Waqf)
docs.text: Character Name Diacritic-Insensitive Broad ۖ Saktah Kept Removed ۗ Waqf Kept Removed ۘ Qif Kept Removed ۙ Waqf Murakhkhas Kept Removed ۚ Waqf Mu'annaq Kept Removed ۛ Waqf Mutalaq Kept Removed

docs.title: Search Result Metadata
docs.text:
Every search result includes normalization metadata:

results = quran.search("الرحمن", mode="broad")

for result in results:
    print(f"Reference: {result.reference}")
    print(f"Text: {result.text}")              # Original text
    print(f"Normalized: {result.normalized}")  # Normalized text
    print(f"Mode: {result.mode}")              # Profile used
    print(f"Score: {result.score}")            # Match score
    print(f"Mappings: {result.mappings}")      # Char position mappings

docs.title: Offset Mapping
docs.text:
Track positions between original and normalized text:

# Get mappings for an ayah
ayah = quran.ayah(1, 1)
mappings = quran.get_normalization_mappings(ayah.reference, "broad")

for mapping in mappings:
    print(f"Orig[{mapping.original_start}:{mapping.original_end}] = "
          f"Norm[{mapping.normalized_start}:{mapping.normalized_end}]")

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always specify normalization mode — Don't rely on defaults
  2. Use exact search for verification — Confirm matches with original text
  3. Preserve mappings for highlights — Use mappings to highlight matches in original text
  4. Document your profile choice — Record which profile was used in research
  5. Test edge cases — Verify behavior with hamza, alif maqsurah, ta marbutah

docs.title: Dataset Management
docs.text: QuranKit uses a dataset registry system for managing Qur'anic text, morphology, and lexical datasets with full provenance tracking.

docs.text:
from qurankit.datasets import DatasetManifest, DatasetValidator
from qurankit.datasets.import_pipeline import ImportPipeline

# Create manifest for custom dataset
manifest = DatasetManifest(
    dataset_id="custom-text",
    name="Custom Qur'an Text",
    version="1.0.0",
    source="My Organization",
    source_url="https://example.com/dataset",
    license="CC-BY-4.0",
    license_url="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/",
    redistribution_status="allowed",
    surah_count=114,
    ayah_count=6236,
    word_count=77430,
    checksum="sha256:...",
    description="Custom text edition for research"
)

# Validate
validator = DatasetValidator()
validation = validator.validate(manifest, dataset_path)
if validation.is_valid:
    # Import
    pipeline = ImportPipeline(quran.config)
    pipeline.import_text_dataset(manifest, dataset_path)
else:
    for error in validation.errors:
        print(f"Validation error: {error}")

# Check license compatibility
from qurankit.datasets.manifest import RedistributionStatus

docs.title: Mutashabihat Analysis
docs.text: QuranKit provides tools for analyzing repeated expressions and textual relationships in the Qur'an (mutashabihat).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The mutashabihat engine detects:

  • Exact repeated phrases — Identical word sequences
  • Near-duplicate phrases — Similar phrases with minor variations
  • Similar openings/endings — Shared beginnings or endings of ayahs
  • Recurring expressions — Phrases appearing multiple times across the corpus

All results are classified by method and confidence level.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from qurankit import Quran

quran = Quran.load()
engine = quran.mutashabihat

docs.title: Exact Repeated Phrases
docs.text:
# Find exact repeated phrases (minimum 2 words)
matches = engine.find_exact_phrases(min_length=2)

for match in matches:
    print(f"Phrase: '{match.text}' (length: {match.length} words)")
    print(f"  Occurs {match.count} times")
    for occ in match.occurrences[:5]:
        print(f"    {occ.reference}: {occ.context}")
    print()

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
# Minimum phrase length (words)
matches = engine.find_exact_phrases(min_length=3)

# Maximum phrase length
matches = engine.find_exact_phrases(min_length=2, max_length=10)

# Minimum occurrences
matches = engine.find_exact_phrases(min_length=2, min_occurrences=3)

# Limit to specific surahs
matches = engine.find_exact_phrases(min_length=2, surahs=[1, 2, 3])

# Exclude common stopwords
matches = engine.find_exact_phrases(min_length=2, exclude_stopwords=True)

docs.title: Near-Duplicate Phrases
docs.text:
# Find phrases with minor variations (Levenshtein distance)
matches = engine.find_near_duplicates(
    min_length=3,
    max_distance=2,  # Max edit distance
    min_occurrences=2
)

for match in matches:
    print(f"Base: '{match.base_text}'")
    for variant in match.variants:
        print(f"  Variant (dist={variant.distance}): '{variant.text}'")
        for occ in variant.occurrences:
            print(f"    {occ.reference}")

docs.title: Similar Openings
docs.text:
# Find ayahs with similar openings to a reference
openings = engine.find_similar_openings(1, 1, max_distance=2)

for opening in openings:
    print(f"{opening.reference}: '{opening.text}' "
          f"(distance: {opening.distance})")

# Compare openings across surahs
surah_openings = engine.compare_surah_openings([1, 2, 3], max_words=5)
for comp in surah_openings:
    print(f"Surah {comp.surah}: '{comp.opening}'")

docs.title: Similar Endings
docs.text:
# Find ayahs with similar endings
endings = engine.find_similar_endings(2, 255, max_distance=2)

for ending in endings:
    print(f"{ending.reference}: '{ending.text}' "
          f"(distance: {ending.distance})")

docs.title: Recurring Expressions
docs.text:
# Find expressions that recur across the corpus
expressions = engine.find_recurring_expressions(
    min_occurrences=3,
    min_length=2,
    max_length=8
)

for expr in expressions:
    print(f"'{expr.text}' occurs {expr.count} times")
    print(f"  Surahs: {expr.surahs_covered}")
    for occ in expr.occurrences[:3]:
        print(f"    {occ.reference}")

docs.title: Shared Root/Lemma Analysis
docs.text:
# Find ayahs sharing roots with a reference ayah
shared = engine.find_shared_roots(2, 255, min_shared=2)

for item in shared:
    print(f"{item.reference}: {item.shared_roots} shared roots")
    for root in item.roots:
        print(f"  {root}: {root.count} occurrences")

# Find ayahs sharing lemmas
shared = engine.find_shared_lemmas(2, 255, min_shared=2)

docs.title: Word Order Variation
docs.text:
# Find phrases with same words but different order
variations = engine.find_word_order_variations(
    reference=(2, 255),
    window=5
)

for var in variations:
    print(f"{var.reference}: '{var.text}' "
          f"(similarity: {var.similarity:.2f})")

docs.title: Result Classification
docs.text:
All mutashabihat results include classification:

matches = engine.find_exact_phrases(min_length=3)

for match in matches:
    print(f"Method: {match.method}")           # "exact_phrase"
    print(f"Category: {match.category}")       # "deterministic_result"
    print(f"Confidence: {match.confidence}")   # "high"
    print(f"Algorithm version: {match.algorithm_version}")
Category Meaning deterministic_result Reproducible computational result computational_suggestion Candidate requiring validation source_annotation From a sourced dataset

docs.title: Comparison Reports
docs.text:
from qurankit.analysis.reports import ComparisonReport

# Generate detailed comparison report
report = ComparisonReport.generate(
    quran,
    reference=(2, 255),
    include_mutashabihat=True,
    include_shared_roots=True,
    include_shared_lemmas=True,
    include_near_duplicates=True
)

# Export to various formats
print(report.to_markdown())
report.to_json("ayat_kursi_report.json")
report.to_csv("ayat_kursi_report.csv")

# Summary statistics
print(f"Exact phrases: {report.exact_phrase_count}")
print(f"Near duplicates: {report.near_duplicate_count}")
print(f"Shared roots: {report.shared_root_count}")
print(f"Shared lemmas: {report.shared_lemma_count}")

docs.title: Corpus-Wide Statistics
docs.text:
from qurankit.analysis.reports import CorpusStatistics

stats = CorpusStatistics.compute(quran)

print(f"Total surahs: {stats.total_surahs}")
print(f"Total ayahs: {stats.total_ayahs}")
print(f"Total words: {stats.total_words}")
print(f"Unique roots: {stats.unique_roots}")
print(f"Unique lemmas: {stats.unique_lemmas}")
print(f"Repeated phrases (≥3 words, ≥2 occ): {stats.repeated_phrase_count}")
print(f"Most repeated phrase: '{stats.most_repeated_phrase.text}' ({stats.most_repeated_phrase.count}x)")

# Surah-level statistics
for surah_stat in stats.surah_statistics:
    print(f"Surah {surah_stat.number}: {surah_stat.ayah_count} ayahs, "
          f"{surah_stat.word_count} words, {surah_stat.unique_roots} roots")

docs.title: CLI Mutashabihat Commands
docs.text:
# Exact repeated phrases
qurankit mutashabihat phrases --min-length 2 --min-occurrences 3

# Similar to specific ayah
qurankit mutashabihat similar 2:255 --type openings --max-distance 2
qurankit mutashabihat similar 2:255 --type endings --max-distance 2

# Recurring expressions
qurankit mutashabihat recurring --min-length 2 --min-occurrences 3

# Shared roots with ayah
qurankit mutashabihat shared-roots 2:255 --min-shared 2

# Comparison report
qurankit mutashabihat report 2:255 --output report.md

# Corpus statistics
qurankit mutashabihat stats

docs.title: Research Methodology
docs.text:
When using mutashabihat results in research:

  1. Classify results — Always note the method and category
  2. Verify manually — Check a sample of results against the text
  3. Report parameters — Document min_length, max_distance, etc.
  4. Avoid overinterpretation — Similarity ≠ semantic/theological equivalence
  5. Cite sources — Reference the text edition and algorithm version
# Good research practice
results = engine.find_exact_phrases(min_length=3, min_occurrences=2)

# Document parameters
metadata = {
    "method": "exact_phrase_matching",
    "min_length": 3,
    "min_occurrences": 2,
    "text_edition": quran.current_edition.id,
    "algorithm_version": engine.version,
    "date": "2024-01-15"
}

# Report with caveats
print("Note: Exact phrase repetition does not imply interpretive equivalence.")
print("Results are deterministic textual matches requiring scholarly review.")

docs.title: Computational Research
docs.text: QuranKit provides tools for reproducible computational and statistical analysis of Qur'anic text.

docs.title: 1. Semantic Relation Lookup
docs.text:
Find synonyms, antonyms, and other semantic relations from dictionary sources (Lane's Lexicon, Al-Mufradat, etc.).

from qurankit import Quran
from qurankit.analysis import SemanticRelationExtractor, SemanticRelationType

quran = Quran.load()

# Via vocabulary (uses dictionary adapters)
extractor = SemanticRelationExtractor()

# Find synonyms for a root
synonyms = extractor.find_synonyms(root_form="ر ح م")
for rel in synonyms:
    print(f"{rel.subject_headword} → {rel.object_headword} ({rel.relation_type.value})")

# Find antonyms for a lemma
antonyms = extractor.find_antonyms(lemma_form="رحمة")
for rel in antonyms:
    print(f"{rel.subject_headword} → {rel.object_headword} ({rel.relation_type.value})")

# Find all relations for a root
relations = extractor.find_relations_for_root(
    "ر ح م",
    relation_types=[SemanticRelationType.SYNONYM, SemanticRelationType.ANTONYM, SemanticRelationType.RELATED]
)

CLI: 

qurankit research semantic-relations "ر ح م" --type synonym
qurankit research semantic-relations --lemma "رحمة" --type antonym

docs.title: 2. Collocation Analysis
docs.text:
Compute statistically significant word co-occurrences using PMI, Dice coefficient, log-likelihood, or raw frequency.

from qurankit.analysis import CollocationAnalyzer, CooccurrenceMeasure

analyzer = CollocationAnalyzer(edition_id="tanzil-uthmani-v1")

# Corpus-wide collocations
results = analyzer.compute_collocations(
    window_size=5,
    min_cooccurrence=3,
    measure=CooccurrenceMeasure.PMI,
    top_n=50,
    filter_stopwords=True,
)

for r in results:
    print(f"{r.word1} — {r.word2}: PMI={r.score:.4f} (co-occur: {r.cooccurrence_count})")

# Collocations for a specific word
word_colloc = analyzer.get_collocations_for_word(
    "الْحَمْدُ",
    measure=CooccurrenceMeasure.DICE,
    top_n=20
)

CLI: 

qurankit research collocations --top 50 --measure pmi
qurankit research collocations-for "الْحَمْدُ" --measure dice --top 20

docs.title: 3. Cross-Reference Analysis
docs.text:
Find explicit (dataset-annotated) or implicit (computed) links between ayahs.

from qurankit.analysis import CrossReferenceAnalyzer

analyzer = CrossReferenceAnalyzer(edition_id="tanzil-uthmani-v1")

# Implicit links from shared vocabulary (QAC morphology)
links = analyzer.find_implicit_links(
    "2:255",  # Ayat al-Kursi
    min_shared_roots=2,
    min_shared_lemmas=1,
    limit=20
)

for link in links:
    print(f"{link.source_reference} → {link.target_reference}")
    print(f"  Evidence: {link.evidence}")
    print(f"  Confidence: {link.confidence:.2f}")

# Explicit cross-references (requires annotated dataset)
explicit = analyzer.get_explicit_cross_references("2:255")

CLI: 

qurankit research cross-refs "2:255" --implicit --limit 10
qurankit research cross-refs "2:255" --explicit

docs.title: 4. Wujuh wa Nazair Detection
docs.text:
Find candidate verse pairs with similar wording but potentially different meanings (computational approximation for scholarly review).

from qurankit.analysis import WujuhWaNazairAnalyzer

analyzer = WujuhWaNazairAnalyzer(edition_id="tanzil-uthmani-v1")

# For a specific ayah
candidates = analyzer.find_for_reference(
    "2:255",
    min_shared_words=2,
    max_candidates=20
)

for pair in candidates:
    print(f"{pair.ayah1_reference} ~ {pair.ayah2_reference}")
    print(f"  Similarity: {pair.similarity_score:.3f}")
    print(f"  Shared: {', '.join(pair.shared_words[:5])}")

# Corpus-wide candidates
all_candidates = analyzer.find_candidates(
    min_shared_words=3,
    max_candidates=100,
    similarity_threshold=0.4
)

CLI: 

qurankit research wujuh-wa-nazair "2:255" --limit 20
qurankit research wujuh-wa-nazair --limit 100  # Corpus-wide

docs.title: 5. Mutashabihat (Repeated Phrase Detection)
docs.text:
from qurankit.analysis import MutashabihatEngine, MatchMethod

engine = MutashabihatEngine()

# Exact phrase matches
result = engine.find_exact_phrase("2:255", min_length=2)

# Normalized exact matches
result = engine.find_normalized_matches(
    "2:255",
    normalization_profile="diacritics-insensitive-v1",
    min_words=2
)

# Near-duplicate detection (computational suggestion)
result = engine.find_near_duplicates(
    "2:255",
    threshold=0.7,
    normalization_profile="search-broad-v1"
)

# Recurring n-grams
ngrams = engine.find_exact_ngrams(n=3, min_occurrences=2)

# Similar openings/endings
openings = engine.find_similar_openings(prefix_length=3, min_occurrences=2)
endings = engine.find_similar_endings(suffix_length=3, min_occurrences=2)

# Recurring expressions
expressions = engine.find_recurring_expressions(min_length=3, min_occurrences=3)

docs.title: 6. Comparison Reports
docs.text:
from qurankit.analysis import ReportGenerator

reporter = ReportGenerator()

# Single ayah report
report = reporter.generate_report(result, "tanzil-uthmani-v1", "2:255")
print(reporter.format_report_text(report))

# Multi-ayah reports
reports = reporter.generate_multi_report(["2:255", "3:2", "1:1"])

# Corpus statistics
stats = reporter.generate_corpus_statistics()
print(stats)

docs.title: 7. Vocabulary & Frequency Analysis
docs.text:
from qurankit import Quran

quran = Quran.load()
vocab = quran.vocabulary

# Root frequency list
roots = vocab.get_root_frequency_list(min_occurrences=10, limit=50)
for r in roots:
    print(f"{r['root_form']}: {r['frequency']} (surahs: {r['surah_count']})")

# Lemma frequency list
lemmas = vocab.get_lemma_frequency_list(min_occurrences=5, limit=50)

# Vocabulary statistics
stats = vocab.get_vocabulary_stats(root_form="ر ح م")
print(f"Total: {stats.total_occurrences}, Surahs: {stats.unique_surahs}")

# Concordance
concordance = vocab.get_concordance(root_form="ر ح م", context_words=3, limit=20)
for line in concordance:
    print(f"{line['reference']}: ...{line['target_form']}...")

# Root/lemma/surface lookup
occurrences = vocab.get_occurrences_by_root("ر ح م")
occurrences = vocab.get_occurrences_by_lemma("رحمة")
occurrences = vocab.get_occurrences_by_surface("رحمن")

docs.title: Claim Categories
docs.text:
Every result is tagged with a claim category per AGENTS.md:

Category Description Examples source_text Original Qur'anic text Ayah text, surah names source_annotation Imported scholarly data Tafsir, morphology, dictionary senses deterministic_result Exact computation Exact phrase match, n-grams computational_suggestion Statistical/algorithmic PMI collocations, near-duplicates research_hypothesis Exploratory findings Wujuh wa Nazair candidates

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
from qurankit.models.research import ResearchRun, ResearchResult, ClaimCategory
from datetime import datetime, UTC

run = ResearchRun(
    run_id="my_analysis_001",

    algorithm_version="0.3.0",

        "window_size": 5,
        "measure": "pmi",
        "min_cooccurrence": 3
    },
    normalization_profile_id="diacritics-insensitive-v1",
    software_version="qurankit-core-0.3.0",
    started_at=datetime.now(UTC),
    status="completed"

result = ResearchResult(
    result_id="colloc_001",
    run_id=run.run_id,
    result_type="collocation_list",
    claim_category=ClaimCategory.DETERMINISTIC_RESULT,
    result_payload_json={"top_10": [...]},
    evidence_json={"method": "PMI", "corpus": "tanzil-uthmani-v1"},
)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always check claim categories — Don't present computational suggestions as facts
  2. Document data sources — Note which datasets/editions were used
  3. Use normalization profiles explicitly — Report which profile was used for search/matching
  4. Validate with multiple methods — Cross-reference PMI with Dice, exact with normalized
  5. Scholarly review required — Wujuh wa Nazair and implicit cross-refs need expert review
  6. Preserve provenance — Every result traces back to source datasets

docs.title: Search & Normalization
docs.text: QuranKit provides powerful search capabilities with explicit normalization profiles.

docs.title: Search Modes
docs.text: Mode Profile Use Case exact Exact Source Verification, citation canonical Canonical Unicode Unicode-normalized comparison diacritic_insensitive Diacritic-Insensitive General search, ignores harakat broad Broad Search Discovery, finds all variants

docs.title: Basic Search
docs.text:
from qurankit import Quran

quran = Quran.load()

# Simple search
results = quran.search("بسم الله")

# With explicit mode

# Limit results

docs.title: Search Results
docs.text:
results = quran.search("كتاب", mode="broad")

for result in results:
    print(f"Reference: {result.reference}")        # e.g., "2:2"
    print(f"Surah: {result.surah_number}")         # 2
    print(f"Ayah: {result.ayah_number}")           # 2
    print(f"Text: {result.text}")                  # Original text
    print(f"Normalized: {result.normalized}")      # Normalized match
    print(f"Mode: {result.mode}")                  # "broad"
    print(f"Score: {result.score}")                # Relevance score
    print(f"Match type: {result.match_type}")      # "exact", "phrase", "token"
    print(f"Mappings: {result.mappings}")          # Char position mappings
    print("---")

results = quran.search("بسم الله الرحمن", mode="exact")

# Find all occurrences of a word form
results = quran.search("رحمن", mode="broad")

occurrences = vocab.lookup_root("ر ح م")
for occ in occurrences:

# Find by lemma

for occ in occurrences:

from qurankit.search import SearchOptions

options = SearchOptions(
    mode="broad",
    limit=100,
    offset=0,
    surah=None,           # Filter by surah
    juz=None,             # Filter by juz
    include_text=True,    # Include full text in results
    include_mappings=True, # Include char position mappings
    min_score=0.0,        # Minimum relevance score
)

results = quran.search("كتاب", options=options)

docs.title: Search Result Types
docs.text: Match Type Description exact Exact character match in original text normalized Match after normalization phrase Multi-word phrase match token Single word token match root Match by root (via vocabulary) lemma Match by lemma (via vocabulary) fuzzy Approximate/fuzzy match (future)

docs.title: Filtering Results
docs.text:
# Filter by surah
results = [r for r in results if r.surah_number == 2]

# Filter by juz
results = [r for r in results if r.juz == 1]

docs.title: Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• FTS5 backend — Uses SQLite FTS5 for fast full-text search
  • Indexes — Search indexes built during dataset import
  • Caching — Results cached for repeated queries
  • Streaming — Large result sets streamed via generators
# Stream large results
for result in quran.search_stream("كتاب", mode="broad"):
    process(result)

# Get count without fetching all
count = quran.search_count("كتاب", mode="broad")

docs.title: Search Statistics
docs.text:
stats = quran.get_search_stats()
print(f"Total documents: {stats.total_documents}")
print(f"Total tokens: {stats.total_tokens}")
print(f"Index size: {stats.index_size_mb} MB")
print(f"Last updated: {stats.last_updated}")

docs.title: Custom Search Profiles
docs.text:
from qurankit.search.normalization import NormalizationProfile, NormalizationRule

# Create research-specific profile
research_profile = NormalizationProfile(
    name="research",
    description="Research profile: keeps Quranic marks, normalizes hamza/ya/ta",
    rules=[
        NormalizationRule.normalize_hamza(),
        NormalizationRule.normalize_ya_maqsurah(),
        NormalizationRule.normalize_ta_marbutah(),
        NormalizationRule.remove_tatweel(),
        # Keep diacritics and Quranic marks for research
    ]
)

quran.search_engine.register_profile(research_profile)
results = quran.search("الرحمن", mode="research")

docs.title: Qur'anic Text Access
docs.text: QuranKit provides structured access to Qur'anic text with full provenance tracking.

docs.title: Text Editions
docs.text:
A TextEdition represents a specific digital representation of the Qur'anic text. Different editions may have:

  • Different orthographies (Uthmani vs. Imlai)
  • Different diacritic markings
  • Different verse numbering (though standard is 114 surahs, 6236 ayahs)
  • Different word tokenization
from qurankit import Quran

quran = Quran.load()

# List available editions
for edition in quran.available_editions:
    print(f"{edition.id}: {edition.name} ({edition.language})")
    print(f"  Source: {edition.source}")
    print(f"  Version: {edition.version}")

# Switch edition
quran.set_edition("tanzil-uthmani")

docs.title: Surah
docs.text:
A Surah represents a chapter of the Qur'an:

surah = quran.surah(1)  # Al-Fatihah

# Properties
print(surah.number)           # 1
print(surah.name_arabic)      # الفاتحة
print(surah.name_english)     # Al-Fatihah
print(surah.name_transliteration)  # Al-Fatihah
print(surah.revelation_type)  # "Makki" or "Madani"
print(surah.ayah_count)       # 7
print(surah.bismillah)        # True/False

# Access ayahs
for ayah in surah.ayahs:
    print(ayah.reference, ayah.text_original)

# Get specific ayah
ayah = surah.ayah(1)

docs.title: Ayah
docs.text:
An Ayah represents a verse:

ayah = quran.ayah(2, 255)  # Ayat al-Kursi

# Properties
print(ayah.surah_number)    # 2
print(ayah.number)          # 255
print(ayah.reference)       # "2:255"
print(ayah.text_original)   # Original Arabic text
print(ayah.text_normalized) # Normalized for search
print(ayah.juz)             # Juz number
print(ayah.hizb)            # Hizb number
print(ayah.rub)             # Rub' number
print(ayah.page)            # Page number (if available)
print(ayah.sajdah)          # True if sajdah verse

# Word tokens (if available)
for token in ayah.word_tokens:
    print(token.position, token.text_original, token.lemma, token.root)

docs.title: WordToken
docs.text:
A WordToken represents a single word occurrence:

token = ayah.word_tokens[0]

# Properties
print(token.id)                    # Unique token ID
print(token.position)              # Position in ayah (1-based)
print(token.text_original)         # Original surface form
print(token.text_normalized)       # Normalized form
print(token.lemma)                 # Lemma (if available)
print(token.root)                  # Root (if available)
print(token.pos)                   # Part of speech (if available)
print(token.morphology)            # Full morphology (if available)
print(token.surah_number)          # Surah number
print(token.ayah_number)           # Ayah number
print(token.char_start)            # Character offset in ayah
print(token.char_end)              # Character offset in ayah

docs.title: Automatic Loading
docs.text:
# Loads first available edition
quran = Quran.load()

# Load specific edition
quran = Quran.load(edition="tanzil-simple")

# Load with custom config
from qurankit import QuranKitConfig
config = QuranKitConfig(data_dir="/custom/path")
quran = Quran.load(config=config)

docs.title: Manual Dataset Installation
docs.text:
# Install Tanzil simple edition
qurankit dataset install tanzil --edition simple --version 1.0.0

# Install Tanzil Uthmani edition
qurankit dataset install tanzil --edition uthmani --version 1.0.0

# List installed datasets
qurankit dataset list

docs.title: Text Integrity Guarantees
docs.text:
QuranKit maintains strict text integrity:

  1. Original text is never modified — text_original preserves the exact source
  2. Normalized text is separate — text_normalized is derived for search
  3. Edition is always tracked — Every text record knows its source edition
  4. Checksums verified — Dataset manifests include SHA-256 checksums
# Verify text integrity
ayah = quran.ayah(1, 1)
print(ayah.text_original)      # Exact source text
print(ayah.edition_id)         # Which edition this comes from
print(ayah.dataset_version)    # Dataset version
print(ayah.checksum)           # SHA-256 of original text

docs.title: Structural Navigation
docs.text:
# By Juz
juz_1 = quran.get_juz(1)
for ayah in juz_1.ayahs:
    print(ayah.reference)

# By Hizb
hizb_1 = quran.get_hizb(1)

# By Page
page_1 = quran.get_page(1)

# By Sajdah
sajdah_ayahs = quran.get_sajdah_ayahs()
for ayah in sajdah_ayahs:
    print(ayah.reference, "(sajdah)")

# Get ayahs in range
ayahs = quran.get_ayahs_range(2, 255, 2, 260)
for ayah in ayahs:
    print(ayah.reference)

docs.title: Multiple Editions Comparison
docs.text:
# Compare same ayah across editions
editions = ["tanzil-simple", "tanzil-uthmani"]
for edition_id in editions:
    quran.set_edition(edition_id)
    ayah = quran.ayah(1, 1)
    print(f"{edition_id}: {ayah.text_original}")

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
• Use quran.surah(n).ayahs for iteration (lazy loading)
  • Access ayah.word_tokens only when needed (may trigger additional loads)
  • Cache frequently accessed data: quran.enable_cache()
  • Use search for bulk retrieval instead of iteration

docs.title: Vocabulary & Lexicon
docs.text: QuranKit provides vocabulary analysis through the QuranicVocabulary class, which integrates with sourced morphological annotations (QAC) and dictionary adapters.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The vocabulary system provides:

  • Root lookup — Find all Qur'anic occurrences of an Arabic root
  • Lemma lookup — Find all occurrences of a lemma
  • Surface form lookup — Find exact word form occurrences
  • Frequency analysis — Corpus-wide root/lemma frequency lists
  • Concordance — Context lines with surrounding words
  • Statistics — Distribution, first/last occurrence, surah coverage

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vocabulary analysis requires QAC morphology data:

# Install QAC morphology dataset
qurankit dataset install qac --version 2.0

Then load Quran with QAC data:

from qurankit import Quran

quran = Quran.load()  # Automatically loads QAC if available
vocab = quran.vocabulary

docs.title: Root Lookup
docs.text:
# Find all occurrences of root ر ح م
occurrences = vocab.lookup_root("ر ح م")

for occ in occurrences:
    print(f"{occ.reference}: {occ.surface_form} "
          f"(lemma: {occ.lemma}, pos: {occ.pos})")

# Output:
# 1:1: بِسْمِ (lemma: بِسْمِ, pos: PREP)
# 1:1: اللَّهِ (lemma: اللَّهُ, pos: NOUN)
# 1:1: الرَّحْمَٰنِ (lemma: الرَّحْمَٰنِ, pos: NOUN)
# 1:1: الرَّحِيمِ (lemma: الرَّحِيمِ, pos: NOUN)
# 2:163: إِلَٰهٌ (lemma: إِلَٰهٌ, pos: NOUN)
# ...

docs.title: Root Lookup Options
docs.text:
# Limit results
occurrences = vocab.lookup_root("ر ح م", limit=20)

# Filter by surah
occurrences = vocab.lookup_root("ر ح م", surah=1)

# Filter by part of speech
occurrences = vocab.lookup_root("ر ح م", pos="NOUN")

# Get as generator for large results
for occ in vocab.lookup_root_stream("ر ح م"):
    process(occ)

# Find all occurrences of lemma رَحْمَان
occurrences = vocab.lookup_lemma("رَحْمَان")

for occ in occurrences:
    print(f"{occ.reference}: {occ.surface_form} "
          f"(root: {occ.root})")

docs.title: Surface Form Lookup
docs.text:
# Find exact surface form occurrences
occurrences = vocab.lookup_surface("الرَّحْمَٰنِ")

for occ in occurrences:
    print(f"{occ.reference}: {occ.surface_form} "
          f"(lemma: {occ.lemma}, root: {occ.root})")

docs.title: Vocabulary Statistics
docs.text:
# Get comprehensive statistics for a root
stats = vocab.get_vocabulary_stats("ر ح م")

print(f"Root: {stats.root}")
print(f"Total occurrences: {stats.total_occurrences}")
print(f"Unique lemmas: {stats.unique_lemmas}")
print(f"Unique surface forms: {stats.unique_surface_forms}")
print(f"Surahs covered: {stats.surahs_covered}")
print(f"First occurrence: {stats.first_occurrence}")
print(f"Last occurrence: {stats.last_occurrence}")
print(f"Part of speech distribution: {stats.pos_distribution}")
print(f"Surah distribution: {stats.surah_distribution}")

# Example output:
# Root: ر ح م
# Total occurrences: 339
# Unique lemmas: 12
# Unique surface forms: 45
# Surahs covered: 78
# First occurrence: 1:1
# Last occurrence: 114:6
# POS distribution: {'NOUN': 298, 'VERB': 35, 'ADJ': 6}
# Surah distribution: {1: 4, 2: 15, 3: 8, ...}

docs.title: Concordance (KWIC)
docs.text:
# Get concordance lines with context
concordance = vocab.get_concordance("ر ح م", context=2)

for line in concordance:
    print(f"{line.reference}: "
          f"... {line.before} **{line.target}** {line.after} ...")

# Output:
# 1:1: ... **بِسْمِ** اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ ...
# 1:1: ... بِسْمِ **اللَّهِ** الرَّحْمَٰنِ ...
# 1:1: ... اللَّهُ **الرَّحْمَٰنِ** الرَّحِيمِ ...
# 1:1: ... الرَّحْمَٰنِ **الرَّحِيمِ** ...
# 2:163: ... إِلَٰهٌ **إِلَٰهٌ** وَاحِدٌ ...

# Limit lines

for item in top_roots:

          f"({item.percentage:.2f}%)")

# Output:
# 1. ل ه: 2851 (12.34%)
# 2. ن و ن: 1234 (5.34%)
# 3. ر ح م: 339 (1.47%)

docs.title: Dictionary Integration
docs.text:
QuranKit supports external dictionary data through the adapter interface:

from qurankit.lexicon import DictionaryAdapterRegistry, FileBasedDictionaryAdapter

# Register a dictionary adapter
registry = DictionaryAdapterRegistry()

# Load from JSONL file
adapter = FileBasedDictionaryAdapter(
    path="data/lexicons/lane_lexicon.jsonl",
    source="Lane's Lexicon",
    format="jsonl"
)
registry.register("lane", adapter)

# Or load from SQLite
adapter = FileBasedDictionaryAdapter(
    path="data/lexicons/al_mufradat.db",
    source="Al-Mufradat",
    format="sqlite"
)
registry.register("mufradat", adapter)

# Look up dictionary entries
entries = adapter.lookup_headword("رَحْمَة")
for entry in entries:
    print(f"Headword: {entry.headword}")
    print(f"Root: {entry.root_form}")
    for sense in entry.senses:
        print(f"  Definition: {sense.definition}")

docs.title: JSONL Format
docs.text:
{
  "entry_id": "lane-001",
  "headword": "رَحْمَة",
  "headword_original": "رَحْمَة",
  "root_form": "ر ح م",
  "lemma_form": "رَحْمَة",
  "entry_text_original": "رَحْمَةٌ: رحمة الله: نعمته وإحسانه.",
  "entry_location": "Lane, Vol. 1, p. 345",
  "senses": [
    {
      "sense_id": "lane-001-1",
      "definition": "Mercy, compassion, pity; the mercy of God, His grace, His beneficence.",
      "definition_language": "en",
      "grammatical_info": "noun, feminine",
      "semantic_domain": "divine_attributes"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "source": "Lane's Lexicon",
    "volume": 1,
    "page": 345
  }
}

docs.title: Provenance Tracking
docs.text:
All vocabulary results include provenance:

occurrences = vocab.lookup_root("ر ح م")

for occ in occurrences:
    print(f"Source: {occ.source}")           # "qac"
    print(f"Dataset version: {occ.dataset_version}")  # "2.0"
    print(f"Method: {occ.method}")           # "morphology_lookup"
    print(f"Confidence: {occ.confidence}")   # "high" / "medium" / "low"

docs.text:
• Indexed lookup — Root/lemma/surface lookups use database indexes
  • Caching — Results cached after first query
  • Streaming — Large result sets support generator iteration

# Pre-warm cache for a root

# Get cache stats

print(f"Cached roots: {stats.cached_roots}")
print(f"Cache size: {stats.size_mb} MB")
